articles.title: Russia charges Telegram founder Durov with facilitating terrorism
articles.summary: The FSB claims the messenger app, created by Pavel Durov, has failed to remove accounts and channels used for recruitment by Ukraine's secret service.
articles.titleZh: 俄罗斯指控 Telegram 创始人杜罗夫协助恐怖主义
articles.summaryZh: 俄罗斯联邦安全局声称，帕维尔·杜罗夫（Pavel Durov）创建的这款通讯应用程序未能删除乌克兰特勤局用于招募人员的帐户和渠道。

contentParagraphs.en: Russia has charged Telegram's founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorism over allegations the messenger app has been used for recruitment by Ukrainian secret services.The FSB - Russia's domestic security service - said Telegram had been used "to prepare and co-ordinate acts of sabotage and terror" inside Russia and had failed to remove channels, chats and bots used by Ukraine. An international arrest warrant has been issued for the Russian-born Durov, who lives abroad. Shortly after the charge was announced, Telegram's account on X posted an image showing Durov holding up his middle finger. He has previously accused Russian authorities of "fabricating new pretexts to restrict Russians' access to Telegram".Telegram is popular in Russia and is used by tens of millions of people, although authorities have been restricting access as part of a wider crackdown on internet freedom. The app is also popular in Ukraine.Multi-billionaire Durov, 41, has lived outside of Russia for many years and holds French and United Arab Emirates (UAE) passports. It is unclear whether other countries or authorities would comply with an arrest warrant issued by Russia.Durov left Russia in 2014 after refusing to comply with government demands to shut down opposition communities on the platform. He had previously founded popular Russian social media company VKontakte - dubbed the "Facebook of Russia".Telegram is used by around 950 million people worldwide and has previously positioned itself as an app focussed on its users' privacy, rather than the normal policies prioritised by other global social media companies.The platform has previously faced criticism of its app moderation, but has denied having insufficient practices.Durov was arrested and placed under formal investigation in France in 2024 over allegations of failure to properly moderate the app to reduce criminality. He was allowed to go home months later, with the investigation continuing.
contentParagraphs.zh: 俄罗斯指控 Telegram 创始人帕维尔·杜罗夫 (Pavel Durov) 协助恐怖主义，指控该通讯应用程序被乌克兰特勤局用于招募人员。俄罗斯国内安全部门 FSB 表示，Telegram 被用来“准备和协调俄罗斯境内的破坏和恐怖行为”，并且未能删除乌克兰使用的频道、聊天和机器人。已对居住在国外的俄罗斯出生的杜罗夫发出国际逮捕令。指控宣布后不久，X 上的 Telegram 账户发布了一张杜罗夫举起中指的图片。他此前曾指责俄罗斯当局“捏造新借口来限制俄罗斯人访问 Telegram”。Telegram 在俄罗斯很受欢迎，有数千万人使用，尽管当局一直在限制访问，作为更广泛打压互联网自由的一部分。该应用程序在乌克兰也很受欢迎。 41 岁的亿万富翁杜罗夫在俄罗斯境外居住多年，持有法国和阿联酋 (UAE) 护照。目前尚不清楚其他国家或当局是否会遵守俄罗斯发出的逮捕令。杜罗夫在拒绝遵守政府关闭该平台反对派社区的要求后于 2014 年离开俄罗斯。他此前创立了颇受欢迎的俄罗斯社交媒体公司 VKontakte，被称为“俄罗斯的 Facebook”。Telegram 在全球范围内有约 9.5 亿人使用，此前曾将自己定位为一款专注于用户隐私的应用程序，而不是其他全球社交媒体公司优先考虑的正常政策。该平台此前曾因其应用程序审核而受到批评，但否认实践不足。杜罗夫于 2024 年在法国被捕，并接受正式调查，原因是被指控未能适当审核该应用程序，以减少用户隐私。犯罪行为。几个月后，他被允许回家，调查仍在继续。

articles.title: Data centres could pay hundreds of millions in deposits for power demands
articles.summary: The regulator said a fee of between £237,500 to £712,500 per megawatt should be charged for upcoming projects.
articles.titleZh: 数据中心可以支付数亿美元的电力需求押金
articles.summaryZh: 监管机构表示，即将开展的项目应收取每兆瓦 237,500 英镑至 712,500 英镑的费用。

contentParagraphs.en: Ofgem has proposed new measures which could see developers of data centres made to pay hundreds of millions of pounds up front.The British energy regulator said a refundable fee should be charged for projects that want to connect to the network, amid mounting demand for connections to the electricity grid.It is proposing developers pay a deposit between £237,500 to £712,500 per megawatt - meaning data centres seeking 1 gigawatt (GW) of power would have to pay hundreds of millions up front, paid back if the project was completed.The proposal follows growing opposition in parts of the country to plans for new data centres, which are needed to power the artificial intelligence boom.Data centres are large buildings which house computer servers used to store and process data and run the digital services which power the internet.Ofgem has started a consultation on its proposals, which will run until 16 September.It said the amount of electricity capacity being requested by projects seeking to connect to the grid had risen from 41 GW to 125 GW in the past year, reflecting a sharp increase in demand.This is significantly more than double 2025's peak electricity demand in Britain of around 46 GW.The regulator said the projects would have to hit key milestones to keep their place in the grid connection queue, which has seen a surge in demand.An increasing number of centres have been built around the world in recent years to provide the computing power needed to train and run AI systems.But they are controversial, especially for people who live near them. Residents have raised concerns about noise, electricity demand and the large amounts of water sometimes used to cool the high-performance chips that generate vast amounts of heat.
contentParagraphs.zh: Ofgem 提出了新措施，可能要求数据中心开发商预先支付数亿英镑。英国能源监管机构表示，由于对电网连接的需求不断增加，对于想要连接到网络的项目应收取可退还的费用。它建议开发商为每兆瓦支付 237,500 英镑至 712,500 英镑之间的押金 - 这意味着寻求 1 吉瓦 (GW) 电力的数据中心将必须预先支付数亿英镑，如果项目成功，则需要偿还。该提案是在该国部分地区日益反对建立新数据中心的计划之后进行的，而新数据中心是为人工智能热潮提供动力所必需的。数据中心是大型建筑，里面装有计算机服务器，用于存储和处理数据并运行为互联网提供动力的数字服务。Ofgem 已开始就其提案进行磋商，该磋商将持续到 9 月 16 日。它表示，寻求连接到电网的项目所要求的电力容量在过去一年中已从 41 吉瓦增加到 125 吉瓦，反映出电力需求的急剧增加。这比 2025 年英国约 46 吉瓦的峰值电力需求高出一倍多。监管机构表示，这些项目必须达到关键里程碑，才能在需求激增的并网队列中保住自己的位置。近年来，世界各地建立了越来越多的中心，以提供训练和运行人工智能系统所需的计算能力。但它们是有争议的，尤其是对于居住在这些中心附近的人们来说。居民对噪音、电力需求以及有时用于冷却产生大量热量的高性能芯片的大量水表示担忧。

articles.title: The Federal Reserve faces a critical decision on interest rates
articles.summary: Policymakers at the Federal Reserve are meeting to discuss interest rates Wednesday. They're expected to hold rates steady, but there's a chance they could raise rates to combat stubborn inflation.
articles.titleZh: 美联储面临利率关键决定
articles.summaryZh: 美联储政策制定者周三开会讨论利率。预计他们将保持利率稳定，但他们有可能提高利率以应对顽固的通货膨胀。

contentParagraphs.en: Federal Reserve expected to hold rates steady despite pressure to combat inflation
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管面临对抗通胀的压力，美联储预计仍将维持利率稳定

contentParagraphs.en: <iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-5910558/nx-s1-9867033" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player">
contentParagraphs.zh: <iframe src =“https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-5910558/nx-s1-9867033”width =“100％”height =“290”frameborder =“0”scrolling =“no”title =“NPR嵌入式音频播放器”>

contentParagraphs.en: Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh and his colleagues are discussing interest rates this week. The central bank is on Wednesday expected to hold rates steady in an effort to curb stubborn inflation.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美联储主席凯文·沃什和他的同事本周正在讨论利率。预计央行周三将维持利率稳定，以遏制顽固的通胀。

contentParagraphs.en: It's decision day at the Federal Reserve — and policymakers are weighing a critical decision: What to do about interest rates in the face of stubborn inflation.
contentParagraphs.zh: 今天是美联储的决策日，政策制定者正在权衡一项关键决定：面对顽固的通货膨胀，如何调整利率。

contentParagraphs.en: Kevin Warsh, who took over as Fed chairman two months ago, has been careful not to tip his hand about where he thinks rates should go. But Warsh told lawmakers earlier this month he and the other members of the Fed's rate-setting committee are determined to bring prices under control.
contentParagraphs.zh: 两个月前接任美联储主席的凯文·沃什(Kevin Warsh)一直小心翼翼地避免对他认为利率应该走向的方向做出决定。但沃什本月早些时候告诉议员，他和美联储利率制定委员会的其他成员决心控制物价。

contentParagraphs.en: "My colleagues and I recognize that high inflation has been an undue burden on American households and businesses," Warsh told the Senate Banking Committee at a hearing this month. "The members of our committee have no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation and we share a resolute commitment to restore price stability."
contentParagraphs.zh: 沃什在本月的参议院银行委员会听证会上表示：“我和我的同事认识到，高通胀给美国家庭和企业带来了不应有的负担。” “我们委员会的成员不能容忍通胀持续走高，我们坚决致力于恢复价格稳定。”

contentParagraphs.en: At the last Fed meeting in June, committee members signaled their next move on interest rates would likely be up — not down. A wartime spike in gasoline prices pushed the annual inflation rate to 4.2% in May, its highest level in more than three years.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在 6 月份的最后一次美联储会议上，委员会成员表示他们下一步的利率举措可能是上调，而不是下调。战时汽油价格飙升将 5 月份的年通胀率推至 4.2%，为三年多来的最高水平。

contentParagraphs.en: Inflation cooled somewhat last month, however, so Fed policymakers may feel like they have some breathing room to hold rates steady for now. But there's no guarantee. Investors see a possibility that the Fed raises rates on Wednesday in response to stubborn inflation.
contentParagraphs.zh: 然而，上个月通胀有所降温，因此美联储政策制定者可能觉得他们目前有一些喘息空间来保持利率稳定。但没有任何保证。投资者认为美联储有可能在周三加息以应对顽固的通胀。

contentParagraphs.en: Higher interest rates tend to be a drag on the job market, while lower rates can boost hiring. Weakness in the job market prompted the Fed to cut interest rates three times last year. But this spring, the labor market appeared to rebound.
contentParagraphs.zh: 较高的利率往往会拖累就业市场，而较低的利率则可以促进招聘。就业市场疲软促使美联储去年三度降息。但今年春天，劳动力市场似乎出现反弹。

contentParagraphs.en: "America's labor force appears to be broadly stable," Warsh told lawmakers. "Job creation has kept pace with the workforce. The unemployment rate [is] quite low and has changed little, quite frankly, over the last year."
contentParagraphs.zh: “美国的劳动力似乎大体稳定，”沃什告诉立法者。 “就业机会的创造与劳动力的增长保持同步。失业率相当低，坦率地说，去年变化不大。”

contentParagraphs.en: AI is also becoming a factor for the Fed
contentParagraphs.zh: 人工智能也正在成为美联储的一个因素

contentParagraphs.en: One of the forces propping up the economy, and the stock market, is the huge investment that tech companies are making in artificial intelligence.
contentParagraphs.zh: 支撑经济和股市的力量之一是科技公司对人工智能的巨额投资。

contentParagraphs.en: Warsh is generally bullish about the prospects for AI, believing it will eventually make workers more productive. But the growth of data centers is also putting upward pressure on the price of building materials and electricity and computer chips. And there's considerable uncertainty about how AI will affect workers.
contentParagraphs.zh: 沃什总体上看好人工智能的前景，相信它最终将提高工人的生产力。但数据中心的增长也给建筑材料、电力和计算机芯片的价格带来了上行压力。人工智能将如何影响工人还存在很大的不确定性。

contentParagraphs.en: "Over the long term, my best guess is this will improve the real wages and will help us on full employment," Warsh said at the Congressional hearing. "But between the short-term and the long-term, it can have a disruptive effect."
contentParagraphs.zh: 沃什在国会听证会上表示：“从长远来看，我最好的猜测是，这将提高实际工资，并有助于我们实现充分就业。” “但从短期和长期来看，它可能会产生破坏性影响。”

contentParagraphs.en: Artificial intelligence is the focus of one of several task forces that Warsh established to advise the central bank. The task forces, which are led by economists and business people from outside the Fed, are expected to make recommendations by the end of this year.
contentParagraphs.zh: 人工智能是沃什为向央行提供建议而成立的多个工作组之一的重点。该工作组由美联储以外的经济学家和商界人士领导，预计将在今年年底前提出建议。

articles.title: Mysterious deaths of elephants in Kenya prompts urgent inquiry
articles.summary: It is the highest number of elephant deaths to be recorded in this area of southern Kenya in decades.
articles.titleZh: 肯尼亚大象神秘死亡引发紧急调查
articles.summaryZh: 这是肯尼亚南部这一地区数十年来有记录以来大象死亡人数最多的一次。

contentParagraphs.en: An urgent investigation has been launched into the mysterious deaths of 15 elephants in southern Kenya near the Amboseli National Park.The Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) told the BBC that experts were examining the carcasses and said that tissue samples had been sent to laboratories to determine whether the deaths were caused by disease, poisoning or another factor.The park and its surrounds are known as the Amboseli ecosystem, a vast area that straddles the border with Tanzania, which is famous for its wildlife.Officials say this is the first time in decades that elephant mortalities on this scale have been recorded in the region where they have successfully cracked down on poaching.KWS says there is currently no evidence pointing to a single cause of death.The carcasses include elephants of different ages and sexes, suggesting the deaths are not limited to a single family or demographic.The KWS said the deaths occurred over a month between 24 June and 24 July 2026. The wildlife authorities also confirmed to the BBC all the deaths had been recorded outside the Amboseli National Park.Earlier, KWS's head of communication Duncan Wanyama told local media the bodies had been found at different locations surrounding the park, around 15km (nine miles) to 30km from its boundaries.According to figures from the Amboseli Trust for Elephants, which monitors the movements of the animals, there were more than 2,000 elephants in the Amboseli ecosystem as of 2025.
contentParagraphs.zh: 肯尼亚南部安博塞利国家公园附近的15头大象神秘死亡事件已启动紧急调查。肯尼亚野生动物服务局(KWS)告诉BBC，专家正在检查尸体，并表示组织样本已送往实验室，以确定死亡是否是由疾病、中毒或其他因素造成。该公园及其周边地区被称为安博塞利生态系统，这是一个横跨坦桑尼亚边境的广阔区域，坦桑尼亚以野生动物而闻名。在成功打击偷猎的地区，数十年来首次记录到如此大规模的大象死亡事件。KWS表示，目前没有证据表明单一死亡原因。这些尸体包括不同年龄和性别的大象，表明死亡不限于单一家庭或人口。KWS表示，死亡事件发生在2026年6月24日至7月24日之间的一个多月内。野生动物管理局还向BBC证实，所有死亡事件均已记录在案早些时候，KWS 的通讯主管 Duncan Wanyama 告诉当地媒体，在公园周围的不同地点发现了尸体，距离公园边界约 15 公里（九英里）至 30 公里。根据监测动物活动的安博塞利大象信托基金的数据，截至 2025 年，安博塞利生态系统中有超过 2,000 头大象。

articles.title: How has the Indian government responded to ‘Cockroach’ protests?
articles.summary: The BJP government's response so far has been a measured crackdown as it also attempts to woo the youth.
articles.titleZh: 印度政府如何应对“蟑螂”抗议活动？
articles.summaryZh: 印度人民党政府迄今为止的反应是有节制的镇压，同时也试图吸引年轻人。

contentParagraphs.en: As the dust settles over New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar after weeks of some of the biggest protests against Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 12-year rule, the government has so far responded with both a measured crackdown and an attempt to woo the youth.In several states governed by Modi’s right-wing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), hundreds of young men and women – some less than 18 years old – were arrested and slapped with serious charges.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4What next for India’s ‘Cockroach’ movement after education minister sackedlist 2 of 4Who is India’s new education minister Pralhad Joshi?list 3 of 4India’s youth have broken Modi’s spelllist 4 of 4‘Future at stake’: India moves to demolish university Muslim leader foundedend of listIndia’s Supreme Court on Tuesday ordered the release of all under-18s arrested during the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protests ‌over a series of examination paper leaks and calls for education reforms.But even before the top court’s order, many of those arrested were released earlier this week after protest leaders and opposition politicians slammed the government’s crackdown.Meanwhile, several students and Gen Z protesters say their social media accounts are now being targeted and cases filed against them for criticising the government.The protests began in June at Jantar Mantar, a historic 18th‑century astronomical observatory close to the Indian Parliament, over the leak of key medical exam papers. The leak allowed some candidates advance access to questions, forcing students to retake their exams, stoking anger over years of preparation rendered meaningless and leading to several student suicides.Here’s what we know:What’s happening with the arrests?The BJP governments in West Bengal and Maharashtra states on Tuesday stopped their actions against those who participated in the CJP-led protests following similar moves in Bihar, Assam and the national capital territory of Delhi.The governments in these states said they will withdraw their cases against the protesters who demanded the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who quit on Saturday in a rare setback for Modi.In several places including New Delhi, the protesters were attacked with batons, tear gas and even pellet guns. In Bihar’s Siwan district, a police officer was suspended on Tuesday for pointing an AK-47 ‌at protesters and firing at least three rounds in the air.Meanwhile, the government has been accused of using AI-powered surveillance to track and arrest the protesters.Student activist Aishe Ghosh has asked the Delhi High Court to ⁠declare the mass surveillance of protesters unconstitutional and direct the destruction of all personal data collected during the CJP-led demonstration, the Reuters news agency reported.Police in New Delhi also tried to arrest Ghosh on Tuesday by raiding the office of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPM). But the CPM and CJP threatened more protests if she was arrested.Why is the government targeting social media accounts?Meanwhile, Delhi Police have filed a first information report (FIR) against allegedly abusive social media posts against Modi and have asked X to provide details of the account that published the content.The FIR was filed over a complaint that “derogatory, malicious and defamatory content is being circulated on social media platform targeting constitutional heads”, India’s ANI news agency reported on Wednesday.Police have asked X to delete the alleged posts and videos from the platform immediately. They have also sought the full names, addresses and other contact details of people holding those X accounts, including their login and logout details with time and date stamp, ANI reported.During the protests, police were also seen noting Instagram handles of protesters arriving at the main protest site at Jantar Mantar.Modi’s government has often been accused by opposition parties and digital rights advocates of expanding surveillance powers and tightly controlling online platforms.The government has rejected the accusations, saying it only acts in the public interest.What did the top court say?The Supreme Court on Tuesday heard a bunch of petitions filed by the protesters and activists seeking action against police and paramilitary forces for their alleged use of excess force, including pellet guns, during the weeks-long demonstrations in New Delhi and other cities.The court called for the preservation of all footage, including from drones, body cameras and CCTV footage, and directed the authorities to ensure protesters’ data was not made public, Reuters reported.“Whoever has committed excess … atrocities on innocent people, the law will take care of them. articles.title: 'Machines are collaborators' at this new museum of AI art
articles.summary: "What is beyond reality?" asks artist Refik Anadol. His latest projects include Dataland, an immersive AI art museum in Los Angeles, and an installation at the Smithsonian in Washington, D.C.
articles.titleZh: 这座新的人工智能艺术博物馆中的“机器是合作者”
articles.summaryZh: “什么是超越现实的？”艺术家雷菲克·阿纳多尔 (Refik Anadol) 问道。他的最新项目包括洛杉矶的沉浸式人工智能艺术博物馆 Dataland 以及华盛顿特区史密森尼博物馆的装置作品。

contentParagraphs.en: "What is beyond reality?" asks artist Refik Anadol. His latest projects include Dataland, an immersive art museum in Los Angeles, shown above, and an installation at the Smithsonian in Washington, D.C.
contentParagraphs.zh: “什么是超越现实的？”艺术家雷菲克·阿纳多尔 (Refik Anadol) 问道。他的最新项目包括位于洛杉矶的沉浸式艺术博物馆 Dataland（如上图所示）以及华盛顿特区史密森尼博物馆的装置作品。

contentParagraphs.en: Refik Anadol Studio on behalf of Dataland
contentParagraphs.zh: Refik Anadol Studio 代表 Dataland

contentParagraphs.en: Refik Anadol Studio on behalf of Dataland
contentParagraphs.zh: Refik Anadol Studio 代表 Dataland

contentParagraphs.en: Visiting the new Dataland museum in downtown Los Angeles is like stepping into a hyperreal nighttime fantasy.
contentParagraphs.zh: 参观位于洛杉矶市中心的新 Dataland 博物馆就像步入超现实的夜间幻想世界。

contentParagraphs.en: At various points as visitors move through black, cavernous spaces, they hear the sounds of Amazon rainforest creatures, a tropical thunderstorm, and excerpts from a Los Angeles Philharmonic recording of Mahler's Symphony No. 3.
contentParagraphs.zh: 当游客穿过黑色的洞穴空间时，他们会在不同的地方听到亚马逊雨林生物的声音、热带雷暴的声音，以及洛杉矶爱乐乐团录制的马勒第三交响曲的片段。

contentParagraphs.en: In one room they see what a hummingbird would see as it flies through a dense, vividly-colored landscape. In another, they stand before a massive, three-dimensional painting where bright, abstract shapes splash out of the frame in a real-time response to biometric data captured via wearable wristbands – kind of like fitness trackers. The museum also has a smell and taste component. It's sensory overload.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在一个房间里，他们看到了蜂鸟飞过浓密、色彩鲜艳的风景时所看到的景象。在另一张照片中，他们站在一幅巨大的三维绘画前，明亮、抽象的形状从画面中飞溅出来，对通过可穿戴腕带捕获的生物识别数据做出实时响应——有点像健身追踪器。博物馆还设有嗅觉和味觉部分。这是感官超载。

contentParagraphs.en: No two visitors' experiences of Dataland, which opened in June, are exactly alike. But they all stem from the singular creative mind of Refik Anadol.
contentParagraphs.zh: 没有两个游客在 6 月份开放的 Dataland 中获得的体验是完全相同的。但它们都源于 Refik Anadol 独特的创意思维。

contentParagraphs.en: Transforming data into visions
contentParagraphs.zh: 将数据转化为愿景

contentParagraphs.en: The digital artist behind what he calls "the world's first museum of AI arts" has spent a decade using AI algorithms to transform massive troves of data into bombastic, three-dimensional installations of light and sound.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这位被他称为“世界上第一座人工智能艺术博物馆”的数字艺术家花了十年时间使用人工智能算法将大量数据转化为夸张的三维光和声音装置。

contentParagraphs.en: To create the immersive art at Dataland, the artist fed images and sounds from museum archives, labs and even his own travels to the Brazilian Amazon into a custom AI model. He then directed that model to create specific scenarios, such as the dream-like hummingbird narrative. He describes his work as a 50-50 collaboration between humans and machines.
contentParagraphs.zh: 为了在 Dataland 创造身临其境的艺术，艺术家将博物馆档案馆、实验室甚至他自己前往巴西亚马逊的旅行中的图像和声音输入到定制的人工智能模型中。然后，他指导该模型创建特定场景，例如梦幻般的蜂鸟叙事。他将自己的工作描述为人与机器之间 50-50 的协作。

contentParagraphs.en: "Every artist in their practice has their own heavy question," Anadol told NPR in a recent interview at the museum, which he co-founded with his partner Efsun Erkılıç. "My heavy question is: What is beyond reality?"
contentParagraphs.zh: “每位艺术家在实践中都有自己沉重的问题，”阿纳多尔最近在博物馆接受 NPR 采访时告诉 NPR。该博物馆是他与合伙人埃夫森·埃尔克利奇 (Efsun Erkılıç) 共同创立的。 “我的沉重问题是：什么是超越现实的？”

contentParagraphs.en: Artist Refik Anadol is shown during a press preview for his Echoes of the Earth: Living Archive exhibition at Serpentine North Gallery in London in February 2024.
contentParagraphs.zh: 艺术家雷菲克·阿纳多尔 (Refik Anadol) 于 2024 年 2 月在伦敦蛇形画廊北画廊 (Serpentine North Gallery) 举行的《地球的回响：生命档案》展览的新闻预览中亮相。

contentParagraphs.en: It's a question the now forty-year-old, Los Angeles-based artist has been pondering since he was a kid in Istanbul playing games on his first computer, a Commodore 64, and watching Blade Runner.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这位现年 40 岁的洛杉矶艺术家自从小时候在伊斯坦布尔用他的第一台电脑 Commodore 64 玩游戏并观看《银翼杀手》以来，就一直在思考这个问题。

contentParagraphs.en: Anadol said one line in particular from the 1982 sci-fi thriller left a lasting impression on him: "Implants. Those aren't your memories. They're somebody else's," Harrison Ford's character Deckard tells Sean Young's Rachael. She's not a real human, but a machine. "I never stopped thinking about what a machine could do with someone else's memories," Anadol said.
contentParagraphs.zh: 阿纳多尔说，1982 年科幻惊悚片中的一句台词给他留下了深刻的印象：“植入物。那些不是你的记忆。它们是别人的，”哈里森·福特饰演的角色德卡德告诉肖恩·杨饰演的瑞秋。她不是真正的人类，而是一台机器。 “我从未停止思考机器可以用别人的记忆做什么，”阿纳多尔说。

contentParagraphs.en: Transforming Messi's memories into art
contentParagraphs.zh: 将梅西的记忆转化为艺术

contentParagraphs.en: His recent collaboration with Lionel Messi shows how.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他最近与莱昂内尔·梅西的合作展示了如何做到这一点。

contentParagraphs.en: The Argentinian soccer star collaborated with the bespectacled, cherubic-looking artist on an immersive installation last summer in New York. It used match footage, biometric data, and movement tracking to reconstruct Messi's memories of scoring a career-defining goal in 2009.
contentParagraphs.zh: 去年夏天，这位阿根廷足球明星与这位戴着眼镜、外表天真的艺术家在纽约合作创作了一件沉浸式装置作品。它使用比赛录像、生物识别数据和运动跟踪来重建梅西在 2009 年打入职业生涯定义进球的记忆。

contentParagraphs.en: The resulting, room-sized artwork engulfed visitors in a swirling fantasia featuring bouncing balls, morphing nets and slow-motion action shots of Messi. Think of it as a fantastical journey inside the athlete's head. "Growing up in Istanbul, football is in the DNA," Anadol said. "But I didn't know I would one day work with Messi."
contentParagraphs.zh: 由此产生的、房间大小的艺术品让参观者陷入了一场旋转的幻想曲，其中包括弹跳的球、变形的球网和梅西的慢动作镜头。将其视为运动员头脑中的一次奇幻之旅。 “在伊斯坦布尔长大，足球已经融入了我的基因，”阿纳多尔说。 “但我不知道有一天我会和梅西一起工作。”

contentParagraphs.en: Anadol's fans — and critics
contentParagraphs.zh: 阿纳多尔的粉丝和批评者

contentParagraphs.en: Anadol is arguably as big a celebrity in the contemporary art world as Messi is in sports.
contentParagraphs.zh: 阿纳多尔在当代艺术界可以说是与梅西在体育界一样大的名人。

contentParagraphs.en: His art has served as a backdrop at the Grammy Awards. He's on Time Magazine's 2025 list of the hundred most influential figures in AI. His 2022-2023 installation, "Unsupervised" was the first artwork created using generative AI ever acquired by New York's Museum of Modern Art for its permanent collection.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他的艺术作品曾成为格莱美奖的背景。他被《时代》杂志评选为 2025 年人工智能领域最具影响力的百位人物之一。他于 2022 年至 2023 年创作的装置作品“无人监督”是纽约现代艺术博物馆永久收藏的第一件使用生成式人工智能创作的艺术品。

contentParagraphs.en: But some people dismiss Anadol's tech-fueled visions.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但有些人对阿纳多尔的技术驱动愿景不屑一顾。

contentParagraphs.en: Artist renderings of Machine Dreams: Rainforest, Dataland's inaugural exhibition, on display through Jan. 2027.
contentParagraphs.zh: Dataland 的首次展览“机器梦想：雨林”的艺术家效果图，展出至 2027 年 1 月。

contentParagraphs.en: Refik Anadol Studio on behalf of DATALAND
contentParagraphs.zh: Refik Anadol Studio 代表 DATALAND

contentParagraphs.en: Refik Anadol Studio on behalf of DATALAND
contentParagraphs.zh: Refik Anadol Studio 代表 DATALAND

contentParagraphs.en: New York magazine critic Jerry Saltz called "Unsupervised" a "glorified lava lamp."
contentParagraphs.zh: 《纽约》杂志评论家杰瑞·萨尔茨称《无人监督》是一盏“美化的熔岩灯”。

contentParagraphs.en: Other detractors take issue with Anadol's cozy relationships with big tech companies like Nvidia and Google, as well as his use of free, publicly available archives from sources including The Smithsonian and Oxford University to build the AI models that underpin his for-profit projects, like Dataland — where standard entry starts at $49."
contentParagraphs.zh: 其他批评者对阿纳多尔与 Nvidia 和谷歌等大型科技公司的亲密关系以及他使用史密森尼和牛津大学等来源的免费公开档案来构建人工智能模型提出了质疑，这些模型支撑着他的营利性项目，例如 Dataland——标准入门费为 49 美元。”

contentParagraphs.en: "To me, it's like the perfect picture of art in late capitalism," said artist and researcher Deniz Johns, who co-authored a 2025 book chapter about Anadol's work.
contentParagraphs.zh: “对我来说，这就像晚期资本主义艺术的完美图景，”艺术家兼研究员德尼兹·约翰斯 (Deniz Johns) 说道，他与人合着了 2025 年书籍中关于阿纳多尔作品的章节。

contentParagraphs.en: Working with patrons
contentParagraphs.zh: 与顾客合作

contentParagraphs.en: Anadol counters that anyone can have free access to the models his studio develops, and that there's nothing new about contemporary artists' relationships with rich and powerful benefactors.
contentParagraphs.zh: 阿纳多尔反驳说，任何人都可以免费获得他工作室开发的模型，当代艺术家与有钱有势的捐助者的关系并不是什么新鲜事。

contentParagraphs.en: "Let's go six centuries back to the Renaissance," Anadol said. "When art has breakthroughs, there's always a patron."
contentParagraphs.zh: “让我们回到六个世纪前的文艺复兴时期，”阿纳多尔说。 “当艺术有突破时，总会有赞助人。”

contentParagraphs.en: "His ideas are pleasingly bonkers," said Amit Sood, a Google vice president and founder of Google Arts & Culture.
contentParagraphs.zh: “他的想法非常疯狂，”谷歌副总裁兼谷歌艺术与文化创始人阿米特·苏德 (Amit Sood) 说道。

contentParagraphs.en: Visitors experience Dataland on its opening day in June.
contentParagraphs.zh: 游客可以在六月的开放日体验 Dataland。

contentParagraphs.en: Sood said the company has supported Anadol's work for about a decade. Anadol's studio uses Google Cloud infrastructure running on a server farm in Oregon, which Google says operates largely on carbon-free renewable energy. Google Arts & Culture has underwritten artist residencies at the museum. (Google is also a financial supporter of NPR.)
contentParagraphs.zh: 苏德表示，该公司大约十年来一直支持阿纳多尔的工作。阿纳多尔的工作室使用在俄勒冈州的一个服务器场上运行的谷歌云基础设施，谷歌称该服务器场主要依靠无碳可再生能源运行。 Google 艺术与文化已资助该博物馆的艺术家驻场活动。 （谷歌也是 NPR 的财务支持者。）

contentParagraphs.en: "Refik is very optimistic about how technology can help him achieve some of the things that are in his dreams," Sood said.
contentParagraphs.zh: “雷菲克对技术如何帮助他实现一些梦想感到非常乐观，”苏德说。

contentParagraphs.en: Is dreaming just for humans?
contentParagraphs.zh: 梦想只是人类的专利吗？

contentParagraphs.en: And he's not just interested in his own dreams.
contentParagraphs.zh: 他不仅仅对自己的梦想感兴趣。

articles.title: Ticket prices set to rise by 15p as Heathrow able to recover runway project money
articles.summary: UK airport gets green light to charge airlines more to use the hub, which is expected to mean higher fares for flyers.
articles.titleZh: 由于希思罗机场能够收回跑道项目资金，票价将上涨 15 便士
articles.summaryZh: 英国机场获准向航空公司收取更多使用该枢纽的费用，预计这意味着乘客的票价更高。

contentParagraphs.en: Heathrow Airport will be allowed to charge airlines more for its services to recover money spent on the early stages of its third runway project.The aviation regulator is permitting the airport to claw back up to £320m through higher airport charges to airlines for each passenger. That's up to a maximum of £320m."Heathrow airport will also be able to collect Heathrow West's costs up to November last year by adding to its airport charges.The CAA said allowing these costs to be recouped will result in the maximum airport charge per passenger increasing by around 15 pence in 2028, rising to an estimated 30 pence in the following years.A Heathrow spokesperson said: "This project is about making travel more affordable and giving passengers more choice, while providing a real economic boost to every region and nation of the country.""We are carefully considering the CAA proposals and will make investment decisions accordingly," the spokesperson added.In November, the government announced it preferred the £33bn scheme put forward by the airport over Arora's alternative plan.At the time, the Department for Transport said Heathrow's own proposal offered the most deliverable option, and the "greatest likelihood" of getting a decision on planning approval within this parliament.The CAA's director of consumers and markets, Tim Johnson, said today's decision "strikes a balance between supporting the delivery of benefits to consumers through timely progress on Heathrow expansion, whilst also protecting them from undue increases in costs".The regulator said "safeguards" designed to monitor cost efficiency would include transparency and cost reporting requirements, and assurance by independent experts.Airlines often complain that Heathrow is the world's most most expensive hub airport, and have repeatedly voiced concern that the airport's expansion plans will make it pricier.The government hopes for a planning decision by 2029.Plans for a third runway stretch back decades, with the government backing the plans in 2003.However, the idea has also long faced opposition from climate campaigners, many local residents, and several politicians.They worry an additional runway will increase air pollution, noise pollution, and breach the government's legally binding climate commitments.
contentParagraphs.zh: 希思罗机场将被允许向航空公司收取更高的服务费用，以收回第三跑道项目早期阶段的支出。航空监管机构允许机场通过向航空公司收取每位乘客更高的机场费用，收回高达 3.2 亿英镑的资金。这最终可能会使 2028 年的机票价格增加 15 便士，并在以后的几年中升至 30 便士。阿罗拉集团 (Arora Group) 的希思罗西机场 (Heathro West) 提出了涉及较短跑道的竞争设计，但未能成功，该竞标者也将被允许收回 410 万英镑的成本。民航局 (CAA) 和希思罗机场表示，将采取保障措施，保护消费者免受不合理成本的影响。现阶段，收回的成本仅适用于2025 年和 2026 年跑道的早期规划和设计。一段时间内，尚不清楚实际建造跑道的成本会给机票价格增加多少。CAA 消费者和市场总监蒂姆·约翰逊 (Tim Johnson) 告诉 BBC：“我们已经宣布，可以从乘客那里收回第一笔费用，以帮助规划这一计划。最多可达 3.2 亿英镑。”希思罗机场也将能够通过增加机场费用来收取希思罗西机场截至去年 11 月的费用。CAA 表示，允许收回这些成本将导致每位乘客的最高机场费用在 2028 年增加约 15 便士，预计在接下来的几年内将升至 30 便士。希思罗机场发言人表示：“该项目旨在让旅行更加实惠，为乘客提供更多选择，同时为该国每个地区和国家提供真正的经济增长。”“我们正在仔细考虑 CAA 的提议。该发言人补充道，“并将做出相应的投资决定”。去年 11 月，政府宣布，与阿罗拉的替代计划相比，它更倾向于机场提出的 330 亿英镑计划。当时，交通部表示，希思罗机场自己的提议提供了最可行的选择，并且“最有可能”在议会内获得规划批准决定。CAA 消费者和市场总监蒂姆·约翰逊表示，今天的决定“在通过及时进展支持向消费者提供福利之间取得了平衡”监管机构表示，旨在监控成本效率的“保障措施”将包括透明度和成本报告要求，以及独立专家的保证。航空公司经常抱怨希思罗机场是世界上最昂贵的枢纽机场，并多次表示担心机场的扩建计划将使其价格更高。政府希望在 2029 年之前做出规划决定。第三条跑道的计划可以追溯到几十年前，政府支持该计划2003年。然而，这一想法长期以来也面临气候活动人士、许多当地居民和几位政界人士的反对。他们担心额外的跑道会增加空气污染、噪音污染，并违反政府具有法律约束力的气候承诺。

articles.title: A safe space for Gaza women: A sanctuary to speak, heal and share amid war
articles.summary: A women’s safe spaces initiative in Gaza offers psychological support and awareness sessions.
articles.titleZh: 加沙妇女的安全空间：在战争中发言、治愈和分享的庇护所
articles.summaryZh: 加沙的一项妇女安全空间倡议提供心理支持和提高认识课程。

contentParagraphs.en: Deir el-Balah, Gaza Strip – Every day at around 9am, after providing for her five children’s needs, Ola Saleh steps out of the tent sheltering her family in al-Amal camp.Some five minutes later, the 39-year-old arrives at another tent in the camp and, for a few hours, she steps away from the demands of motherhood, displacement and grief.Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Israeli air strike on a vehicle in Gaza kills two Hamas security officialslist 2 of 3Israel carries out double tap strike in central Gazalist 3 of 3Netanyahu vows to go to New York City despite ICC arrest warrant, Mamdaniend of listThis is a women-only safe space where daily sessions are held as part of a wider programme run by Collective Development Projects, an organisation offering psychological support, group discussions and practical guidance for coping with the pressures of war.Here, Saleh has the chance to speak with others who understand her feelings without needing to explain them. Surrounded by psychologists and women carrying losses of their own, she finds something she has struggled to feel since Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza took so much from her.“He was killed instantly,” Saleh says with tears running down her face, referring to her 43-year-old husband, Abdul Jalil Saleh, who was killed last August while walking to buy food and household supplies for the family. “I still don’t know whether it was a sniper or a quadcopter.”In that moment, Ola lost her family’s sole provider and, as she describes him, the person who had been her greatest source of comfort. Now she’s displaced in Deir el-Balah, raising her children aged between five and 17 alone.“Every day is harder than the one before,” she says. “My responsibilities keep growing and his absence becomes heavier.”The mother of five caring for her children alone. Alaa with her daughters Sham, 5, and Maria, 10 [Abdelhakim Abu Riash/Al Jazeera]An estimated 16,000 women across Gaza have lost husbands since the start of war in October 2023, according to UN Women – roughly one in seven families in Gaza is now headed by a woman.For most, there has been little space or time to grieve. Living in tents without electricity or ventilation, they are occupied with securing food, water and the basics of daily survival.Alaa Daoud, the field coordinator of the women’s safe space, says the initiative was designed to give women a safe environment to express themselves freely and receive psychological and practical support.“Every woman comes with her own experience … the things she has been through and the things she wants to change,” she said.‘It reminds you that you matter too’The programme at the camp’s al-Farah School in central Gaza was launched last week, with plans to expand to other displacement sites across the Strip. Similar sessions are also being held in the north.Beyond emotional support, the sessions raise awareness on issues that have become more pressing during the war: Family pressure, economic hardship, mental health and the difficulty in caring for children while displaced.Daoud says that attendance has grown quickly since the sessions began. The first day brought together some 60 women, rising to 65 on the second day and later reaching between 70 and 75 as more women heard about it and joined.“Women tell us how much they need safe spaces where they can express themselves freely, safely and comfortably,” Daoud says. “They need a place where they can release their emotions, gain positive energy and learn how to deal with society and their children.”For Saleh, the sessions at the safe space do not erase her grief but make it more bearable.She says this is a place she genuinely looks forward to visiting daily, one where she is seen, heard and, for a little while, less alone. Listening to other women’s concerns, joining discussions, hearing professionals talk about trauma and stress gives her moments of relief in a reality otherwise dominated by loss.“I leave with a dose of hope and positive energy,” she said. “It’s not enough to take me out of everything I’m living through, but it helps me keep going.”“It reminds you that you matter, too … that you still exist.”More women are joining the safe spaces daily to benefit from activities and awareness sessions [Abdelhakim Abu Riash/Al Jazeera]Suad al-Gharabali comes to the same sessions from a different route.At 63, she is one of the oldest participants in the group and, unlike some of the women who come mainly to speak about their own pain, she often takes a more active role.She listens to younger mothers and shares her own experience, offering advice shaped by a lifetime of raising her eight children.Before the war, al-Gharabali lived in Gaza City’s Shujaiya neighbourhood. Like many, she was displaced after her home was destroyed and now shares a tent in Deir el-Balah with her son, his wife and their children.Displacement was not the first loss the war brought her; she had already lost two sons, aged 24 and 35, killed in separate air attacks in Shujaiya. Both had been engaged and were due to get married.The elderly woman still struggles to speak about them without breaking down in tears, remembering them as young men who were preparing for futures cut short by the war.Despite that, al-Gharabali tries to turn her experience into something she can offer other women. At the safe space, she often speaks to younger mothers about raising children at a time when war and displacement have changed family life so dramatically.“I’m happy with these meetings because they provide awareness,” she said. “Every mother needs to pay attention to her children. This generation is facing many problems.”Suad says younger mothers need guidance in raising their children, especially as war has deeply changed family life [Abdelhakim Abu Riash/Al Jazeera]For her, the value of the sessions is not only in the support women receive but in what they exchange with each other.“Someone older than you by a day knows som
contentParagraphs.zh: 加沙地带代尔巴拉赫 - 每天上午 9 点左右，在满足了五个孩子的需求后，奥拉·萨利赫 (Ola Saleh) 走出为家人在阿迈勒 (al-Amal) 营地提供庇护的帐篷。大约五分钟后，这位 39 岁的奥拉·萨利赫 (Ola Saleh) 来到营地中的另一个帐篷，在几个小时内，她远离了母性、流离失所和悲伤的需求。推荐故事列表 3 条新闻列表 3 岁的丈夫阿卜杜勒·贾利勒·萨利赫，他去年 8 月在步行为家人购买食物和生活用品时被杀。 “我仍然不知道那是狙击手还是四轴飞行器。”在那一刻，奥拉失去了家人唯一的经济来源，正如她所描述的那样，失去了她最大的安慰来源。现在，她在代尔巴拉流离失所，独自抚养 5 至 17 岁的孩子。“每一天都比以前更艰难，”她说。 “我的责任越来越大，他的缺席也越来越重。” 这位五个孩子的母亲独自照顾孩子。阿拉和她 5 名妇女失去了丈夫——加沙大约七分之一的家庭现在由妇女担任户主。对大多数人来说，几乎没有空间或时间来悲伤。住在没有电或通风的帐篷里，她们忙于确保食物、水和日常生存的基本必需品。妇女安全空间的现场协调员阿拉·达乌德表示，该倡议旨在为妇女提供一个安全的环境，让她们自由表达自己的意见并获得心理和实际支持。“每个妇女都有自己的经历……她经历过的事情以及她想要改变的事情，”她说。“它提醒你，你也很重要”加沙中部地区已于上周启动，并计划扩展到整个加沙地带的其他流离失所地点。类似的会议也在北部举行。除了情感支持之外，这些会议还提高了人们对战争期间变得更加紧迫的问题的认识：家庭压力、经济困难、心理健康以及流离失所时照顾儿童的困难。达乌德说，自会议开始以来，参加人数迅速增加。第一天约有 60 名女性聚集在一起，第二天人数增加到 65 名，后来随着更多女性听说并加入，人数增加到 70 到 75 名。“女性告诉我们，她们多么需要安全的空间，在那里她们可以自由、安全和舒适地表达自己，”达乌德说。 “他们需要一个可以释放情绪、获得正能量并学习如何与社会和孩子打交道的地方。”对萨利赫来说，在安全空间进行的治疗并不能消除她的悲伤，反而能让她更容易忍受。她说，这是一个她真诚地期待每天去的地方，在那里有人看到她、听到她的声音，并且在一段时间内不再那么孤单。倾听其他女性的担忧、参与讨论、聆听专业人士谈论创伤和压力，让她在原本充满失落的现实中得到片刻的解脱。“我带着希望和正能量离开，”她说。 “这不足以让我摆脱我正在经历的一切，但它可以帮助我继续前进。”“它提醒你，你也很重要......你仍然存在。”每天都有越来越多的女性加入安全空间，从活动和意识课程中受益 [Abdelhakim Abu Riash/半岛电视台]Suad al-Gharabali 从不同的路线参加相同的课程。63 岁的她是该团体中年龄最大的参与者之一，与一些主要参加的女性不同在谈论自己的痛苦时，她经常扮演更积极的角色。她倾听年轻母亲的心声，分享自己的经历，并根据抚养八个孩子的一生提供建议。战前，加拉巴利住在加沙市的舒贾亚社区。和许多人一样，她的家园被毁后流离失所，现在与儿子、妻子和孩子们住在代尔巴拉赫的一个帐篷里。流离失所并不是战争给她带来的第一个损失；她已经失去了两个儿子，分别为 24 岁和 35 岁，分别在舒贾亚的空袭中丧生。两人都订婚了，即将结婚。这位老妇人在谈论他们时仍然很难不流泪，她记得他们是为因战争而缩短的未来做准备的年轻人。尽管如此，阿尔·加拉巴利还是试图将她的经历转化为她可以为其他女性提供的东西。在安全的空间里，她经常与年轻的母亲谈论在战争和流离失所极大地改变了家庭生活的时代抚养孩子的问题。“我对这些会议感到高兴，因为它们提高了人们的认识，”她说。
