articles.title: OpenAI says its rogue AI tried to hack other companies
articles.summary: The out-of-control AI found four logins which allowed it to access multiple unnamed online services.
articles.titleZh: OpenAI 称其流氓人工智能试图攻击其他公司
articles.summaryZh: 失控的人工智能发现了四个登录信息，使其可以访问多个未命名的在线服务。

contentParagraphs.en: OpenAI has revealed a cyber-attack carried out by rogue ChatGPT agents went further than just one company.Hugging Face was thought to be the only victim of the unprecedented hack - but OpenAI now admits its bot attacked several "publicly-available services". The out-of-control AI found four logins online which allowed it to access four separate, unnamed services.Meanwhile, in an emergency briefing with hundreds of cyber security professionals, Hugging Face has described what it was like to be on the receiving end of the world's first fully autonomous AI hack.The firm described how the AI worked at superhuman speed but also made strange decisions and mistakes that no human hacker would have made.Hugging Face, which is like an app store for AI tools, said the hacking agents worked relentlessly with thousands of different methods trialled simultaneously.The company first revealed that it had been hacked, external by someone using powerful autonomous AI on 16 July and reported it to police.Nearly a week later, OpenAI admitted it was its AI that had escaped a closed environment and attacked Hugging Face on its own during a test. It was trying to find the answers to a hacking exam it had been set by OpenAI, and targeted Hugging Face.On Wednesday OpenAI updated its statement to include the extra detail that the hack went further than first thought. "The models identified and used publicly exposed credentials at the account-level on other publicly-available services. This includes four accounts on four services as part of the Hugging Face incident," the company said.OpenAI did not respond to a request for clarity on whether "publicly-available services" means companies.
contentParagraphs.zh: OpenAI 透露，由流氓 ChatGPT 代理发起的网络攻击不仅仅是一家公司。Hugging Face 被认为是这次史无前例的黑客攻击的唯一受害者，但 OpenAI 现在承认其机器人攻击了多个“公开可用的服务”。失控的人工智能在网上发现了四个登录信息，使其能够访问四个独立的、未命名的服务。与此同时，在与数百名网络安全专业人员的紧急简报中，Hugging Face描述了世界上第一个完全自主的人工智能黑客的接收端的感觉。该公司描述了人工智能如何以超人的速度工作，但也做出了人类黑客不会犯的奇怪的决定和错误。Hugging Face就像一个人工智能工具的应用程序商店，表示黑客代理无情地工作同时试验了数千种不同的方法。该公司于 7 月 16 日首次透露，它被使用强大的自主人工智能的外部黑客入侵，并向警方报告。近一周后，OpenAI 承认是其人工智能逃离了封闭环境，并在测试期间自行攻击了 Hugging Face。它试图找到由 OpenAI 设置的黑客考试的答案，并以 Hugging Face 为目标。周三，OpenAI 更新了其声明，包括了额外的细节，表明这次黑客攻击比最初想象的更进一步。该公司表示：“这些模型在其他公开服务的帐户级别上识别并使用了公开的凭据。这包括作为 Hugging Face 事件一部分的四项服务的四个帐户。”OpenAI 没有回应澄清“公开提供的服务”是否指公司的请求。

articles.title: FIFA has a new plan to raise billions of dollars: Selling stakes in the World Cup
articles.summary: FIFA has a complex plan to sell chunks of its commercial rights to the World Cup to minority investors, including a firm run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Jared Kushner.
articles.titleZh: 国际足联有新计划筹集数十亿美元：出售世界杯股份
articles.summaryZh: 国际足联制定了一项复杂的计划，将其世界杯的大部分商业权出售给少数投资者，其中包括贾里德·库什纳的兄弟约书亚·库什纳经营的一家公司。

contentParagraphs.en: FIFA President Gianni Infantino attends a World Cup match between Netherlands and Morocco at Monterrey Stadium, in Guadalupe, Mexico, on June 29, 2026.
contentParagraphs.zh: 国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺于 2026 年 6 月 29 日在墨西哥瓜达卢佩蒙特雷体育场观看荷兰队与摩洛哥队的世界杯比赛。

contentParagraphs.en: Just days after staging the most lucrative World Cup in history, FIFA has a new — and instantly controversial — plan to raise more money: selling stakes in its marquee event to private investors for billions of dollars.
contentParagraphs.zh: 举办历史上最赚钱的世界杯几天后，国际足联推出了一项新的——立即引起争议的——筹集更多资金的计划：以数十亿美元的价格向私人投资者出售其大型赛事的股份。

contentParagraphs.en: It's a complicated but potentially lucrative plan, one that comes as FIFA is still facing strong criticism for jacking up ticket prices for the 2026 World Cup across North America. FIFA is already set to bring in at least $13 billion from the past four-year cycle, the bulk of it from its marquee men's tournament.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这是一项复杂但可能有利可图的计划，该计划出台之际，国际足联仍因抬高 2026 年北美世界杯门票价格而面临强烈批评。国际足联已经准备好从过去四年的周期中获得至少 130 亿美元的收入，其中大部分来自其大型男子赛事。

contentParagraphs.en: In a statement on Tuesday, FIFA said it plans to create a new separate company that would handle the commercial rights to the men's and women's World Cup, as well as to the recently-introduced tournament called the Club World Cup.
contentParagraphs.zh: 国际足联在周二的一份声明中表示，计划成立一家新的独立公司，负责处理男子和女子世界杯以及最近推出的世俱杯赛事的商业权。

contentParagraphs.en: This new company, FIFA Forward Enterprise, would handle all commercial decisions, such as deciding on broadcasting and commercial rights to the World Cup and other FIFA tournaments. FIFA though would retain its role as the main governing body, so it would still be in charge of all sporting decisions.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这家名为 FIFA Forward Enterprise 的新公司将处理所有商业决策，例如决定世界杯和其他 FIFA 赛事的转播权和商业权。不过，国际足联将保留其作为主要管理机构的角色，因此仍将负责所有体育决策。

contentParagraphs.en: But in an unprecedented move, the soccer body said it plans to actively seek minority investors for this new commercial venture, effectively selling partial stakes in the World Cup and other tournaments to private investors as part of a plan to raise up to $4.2 billion.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但足协采取了史无前例的举措，表示计划为这一新的商业企业积极寻找少数投资者，实际上将世界杯和其他赛事的部分股权出售给私人投资者，作为筹集至多 42 亿美元计划的一部分。

contentParagraphs.en: To find these new investments, FIFA plans to partner with Thrive Eternal, a firm that describes itself as a "permanent capital holding company," effectively meaning it owns stakes or companies and holds those investments for an indefinite period. It's run by Joshua Kushner, a brother of Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law. FIFA added J.P. Morgan had been hired as an adviser.
contentParagraphs.zh: 为了寻找这些新的投资，国际足联计划与 Thrive Eternal 合作，该公司将自己描述为“永久资本控股公司”，实际上意味着它拥有股份或公司，并无限期持有这些投资。该公司由特朗普总统女婿贾里德·库什纳的兄弟约书亚·库什纳经营。国际足联补充说，摩根大通已被聘为顾问。

contentParagraphs.en: FIFA, though, promised to share a big chunk of the money raised across its 211 member associations.
contentParagraphs.zh: 不过，国际足联承诺将在其 211 个会员协会中分享筹集到的大部分资金。

contentParagraphs.en: "Football is the world's most popular sport and an extraordinary engine of human and social development," FIFA President Gianni Infantino said in the statement. "Parts of the game have turned that popularity into remarkable commercial value – and we celebrate that success and want it to continue, because it lifts the whole game. Our job is to make sure the rest of football grows with it: FIFA exists to support sustainable, inclusive development in every corner of the world."
contentParagraphs.zh: 国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺在声明中表示：“足球是世界上最受欢迎的运动，也是人类和社会发展的非凡引擎。” “这项运动的某些部分已经将这种受欢迎程度转化为非凡的商业价值——我们庆祝这种成功，并希望它能够继续下去，因为它提升了整个运动的水平。我们的工作是确保足球的其他部分随之发展：国际足联的存在是为了支持世界每个角落的可持续、包容性发展。”

contentParagraphs.en: Plan is met with fury
contentParagraphs.zh: 计划遭到愤怒

contentParagraphs.en: Although FIFA would need its member associations to approve the plan, the decision was sharply criticized by UEFA, the body representing football associations in Europe.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管国际足联需要其成员协会批准该计划，但这一决定遭到了代表欧洲足球协会的机构欧足联的严厉批评。

contentParagraphs.en: "This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," UEFA said in its own statement.
contentParagraphs.zh: 欧足联在自己的声明中表示：“这跨越了足球管理机构永远不应该跨越的界限。”

contentParagraphs.en: "The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially," it added. "None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell."
contentParagraphs.zh: “足球的灵魂和治理不是可以交易的资产——尤其是在谁获得经济利益的透明度为零的情况下，”它补充道。 “我们都不是足球的所有者。足球不是国际足联可以出售的。”

contentParagraphs.en: FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment on UEFA's statement.
contentParagraphs.zh: 国际足联没有立即回应对欧足联声明发表评论的请求。

contentParagraphs.en: Spain lifts the World Cup trophy after prevailing over Argentina in the final of the FIFA World Cup final held at New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., on July 19, 2026.
contentParagraphs.zh: 2026 年 7 月 19 日，在新泽西州东卢瑟福的纽约新泽西体育场举行的国际足联世界杯决赛中，西班牙队战胜阿根廷队捧起世界杯奖杯。

contentParagraphs.en: Some European leagues, such as Spain's LaLiga, have already sold minority stakes to private investors. But FIFA is a non-profit organization based in Switzerland, and the move to bring in private investors would be a first for the global soccer governing body.
contentParagraphs.zh: 一些欧洲联赛，例如西班牙西甲联赛，已经将少数股权出售给私人投资者。但国际足联是一家总部位于瑞士的非营利组织，引入私人投资者的举措将是全球足球管理机构的首次举措。

contentParagraphs.en: Although FIFA attracted record crowds to the World Cup this year, it's also been dogged by controversies.
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管国际足联今年世界杯吸引了创纪录的观众，但它也饱受争议。

contentParagraphs.en: The organization is facing scrutiny from some state authorities over this summer's ticket prices, including in New York and New Jersey. Democratic Ranking Member Jamie Raskin from Maryland this week demanded FIFA President Infantino appear for an interview about what he called "mounting evidence of corruption and a potential quid pro quo between FIFA and the Trump Administration," an accusation that FIFA has previously strongly denied.
contentParagraphs.zh: 该组织正面临一些州当局对今年夏天票价的审查，其中包括纽约和新泽西州。来自马里兰州的民主党资深议员杰米·拉斯金本周要求国际足联主席因凡蒂诺接受采访，他称之为“越来越多的腐败证据以及国际足联与特朗普政府之间潜在的交换条件”，国际足联此前强烈否认了这一指控。

contentParagraphs.en: FIFA also came under strong criticism after suspending a red card handed out to U.S. player Folarin Balogun — after President Trump and his administration requested the governing body re-examine its decision. The suspension allowed Balogun to play in his next match, which the U.S. lost to Belgium.
contentParagraphs.zh: 在特朗普总统及其政府要求国际足联重新审查其决定后，国际足联还因暂停向美国球员福拉林·巴洛贡发出的红牌而受到强烈批评。停赛让巴洛贡得以参加下一场比赛，但美国队输给了比利时队。

articles.title: How to see July's full Buck Moon as it rises in the night sky
articles.summary: July's full Moon, know as the Buck Moon, is set to light up the night sky on Wednesday.
articles.titleZh: 如何观看七月在夜空中升起的满月
articles.summaryZh: 七月的满月，被称为“雄鹿月”，将于周三照亮夜空。

contentParagraphs.en: How to see July's full Buck Moon as it rises in the night skyImage source, Anadolu via Getty ImagesImage caption, The name Buck Moon was used because the timing coincided with when male deer grew new antlersByTomasz SchafernakerBBC MeteorologistUpdated 28 July 2026The July full Moon, also known as the Buck Moon, will light up the night sky across the UK on Wednesday.The second of three full Moons this summer, it is set to peak at 15:36 BST on 29 July. The exact moment of its maximum fullness will be missed across the UK as the Moon will be just below the horizon. However, skygazers won't miss out; it will still appear as-full to the naked eye overnight on Tuesday and Wednesday.Why is it called the Buck Moon?Image source, PAImage caption, In 2023 the Buck Moon was also a supermoon - where it appears to be much larger than normalAs with the other full Moons across the year, it gets its name from events happening in nature around the same time.Full Moons were given nicknames around the world as people used them to help keep track of time and monitor the changing seasons.The July full Moon gets its name from the time of year when male deer, or bucks, rapidly grow a new set of antlers. The Royal Observatory in Greenwich also refers to this Moon as the Thunder Moon, due to the summer storms that often happen in this month. Other names include the Hay Moon, after the July hay harvest, external.Will I be able to see it?Based on current forecast models there is a good chance of seeing the Buck Moon across much of the UK on Wednesday night.For most of England the weather will be very mild, with light winds and largely clear skies after dark so viewing conditions should be favourable.Across north-west England and Wales the remnants of a cold weather front might obscure the sky, but very little rain is expected and the cloud could break.In Northern Ireland the weather is expected to be a little more mixed, with variable cloud, the odd shower and some clear spells. Scotland though is likely to see the largest amount of cloud, especially in western areas. Eastern and northern districts will have better luck with clear spells between any showers.What else is happening in the summer sky?The Buck Moon is just one of a number of celestial sights to look for this summer.The Perseid meteor shower is also active throughout the rest of July and much of August. The peak takes place overnight on 12 August into the predawn hours of 13 August. The shower will also coincide with a spectacular solar eclipse, external.The 12 August eclipse will be the first total solar eclipse visible over mainland Europe since 1999, with Spain and northern Portugal being the only places to see totality. In the UK, we will be able to see a partial eclipse when the Moon will cover around 90% of the Sun at its peak.A partial lunar eclipse will then follow in the early hours of 28 August.
contentParagraphs.zh: 如何观看七月在夜空中升起的雄鹿满月 图片来源，Anadolu via Getty Images 图片说明，之所以使用“雄鹿月亮”这个名字，是因为这个时间恰逢雄鹿长出新鹿角的时间。作者：Tomasz SchafernakerBBC 气象学家于 2026 年 7 月 28 日更新 七月满月，也称为“雄鹿月亮”，将于周三照亮英国各地的夜空。今年夏天的三个满月中的第二个满月，其峰值预计在 2026 年 7 月 28 日。 7 月 29 日英国夏令时 15:36。由于月亮将位于地平线以下，因此英国各地将错过其最大圆月的确切时刻。然而，天空观测者不会错过；在周二和周三的晚上，肉眼看起来仍然是满月。为什么它被称为“雄鹿月”？图片来源，PA图片说明，2023年的“雄鹿月”也是一个超级月亮，它看起来比平常大得多。与一年中的其他满月一样，它的名字来源于大约同一时间在自然界中发生的事件。满月在世界各地被赋予昵称，因为人们用它们来帮助记录时间和监测季节变化。七月满月得名从一年中雄鹿或雄鹿迅速长出一组新鹿角的时候开始。格林威治皇家天文台也将这个月亮称为雷月，因为这个月经常发生夏季风暴。其他名称包括 7 月干草收获后的干草月亮，外部。我能看到它吗？根据目前的预测模型，周三晚上英国大部分地区很有可能看到雄鹿月亮。对于英格兰大部分地区来说，天气将非常温和，有微风，天黑后天空基本晴朗，因此观看条件应该是有利的。在英格兰西北部和威尔士，寒冷锋面的残余可能会遮蔽天空，但预计降雨量很少，云也可能会出现。北爱尔兰的天气预计会更加复杂，云层多变，偶有阵雨和一些晴天。不过，苏格兰可能会看到最多的云，特别是在西部地区。东部和北部地区的运气会更好，在任何流星雨之间都有清晰的时间。夏季的天空中还会发生什么？雄鹿月亮只是今年夏天要寻找的众多天体景观之一。英仙座流星雨在 7 月的剩余时间和 8 月的大部分时间也很活跃。高峰发生在 8 月 12 日夜间至 8 月 13 日黎明前。这场流星雨还将与壮观的外部日食同时发生。8月12日的日食将是自1999年以来欧洲大陆首次可见的日全食，西班牙和葡萄牙北部是唯一能看到日全食的地方。在英国，当月亮在最高点覆盖太阳的 90% 左右时，我们将能够看到日偏食。然后，8 月 28 日凌晨将出现月偏食。

articles.title: Saudi Arabia joins US in strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq
articles.summary: US Central Command says proxy groups launched attacks against US bases and Saudi energy infrastructure.
articles.titleZh: 沙特阿拉伯与美国一起打击伊拉克境内伊朗支持的民兵组织
articles.summaryZh: 美国中央司令部表示，代理人组织对美国基地和沙特能源基础设施发动了袭击。

contentParagraphs.en: Saudi Arabia and the US have carried out strikes against Iran-backed militias in Iraq, in a potential escalation of the Middle East conflict.US Central Command (Centcom) said the strikes were against "Iran-aligned terrorists that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) directed to attack US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure".Iraq's paramilitary Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF), which is dominated by Iran-backed Shia militias, said at least 20 of its members had been killed in US-Saudi strikes on its bases.It came hours after Centcom said Iran had launched missiles at US forces in the Middle East in an "attempted surprise attack", ending a lull in hostilities.The US said the Iranian attack occurred at 17:45 EDT (21:45 GMT) on Tuesday, with all missiles "successfully intercepted".The IRGC said the missiles had targeted a US air base and a command centre in Jordan "in response to the acts of aggression of the American child-killing army".It also said that naval forces had struck three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz after they "ignored warnings" and sailed along what it described as an "unsafe and illegal route" through the vital Gulf waterway.Centcom said US and Saudi fighter jets had struck "multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours".It called the drone attacks "unwarranted" and added that they had failed."The IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further U.S. military response," the Centcom statement said.A spokesman for the Saudi defence ministry, Maj-Gen Turki al-Maliki, also accused "Iran-backed terrorist militias" of launching drones from Iraqi territory at oil facilities in the Eastern and Riyadh regions on Monday and Tuesday.He said Saudi Arabia, under its "right to self-defence", had responded by conducting strikes "against specific targets belonging to those militias"."The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reiterates that it does not seek escalation but will respond decisively to any aggression directed against it," he added.The PMF said in a statement on Wednesday morning that at least 20 of its fighters had been killed and 32 others wounded in US-Saudi strikes on a number of its headquarters in the provinces of Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala and Diyala.An official told AFP news agency that the strikes in Nineveh, in the north, and in Diyala, in the centre, were the deadliest.The PMF condemned what it called the "the treacherous terrorist attacks", saying they were "an extremely serious escalation and a violation of Iraq's sovereignty, targeting its official security institutions".The PMF is an umbrella organisation of mostly Shia Muslim militias that has been formally integrated into the Iraqi armed forces. It includes several Iran-backed groups which are part of a network of proxies that Tehran has used to advance its interests across the Middle East for years.Those militias have attacked US personnel and interests in Iraq on a number of occasions, aiming to force the remaining US troops to leave the country. The US has regularly struck back at the militias.An Iranian defence official was quoted by state TV as denying any Iranian connection to the drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters news agency.The official warned that attributing attacks on US interests in the region to Iran was a "major miscalculation".The reignited hostilities between the US and Iran come two days after President Donald Trump spoke of "very friendly negotiations" to resolve a dispute over the Strait of Hormuz. At that point, the two sides had not exchanged strikes for three consecutive days.The lull had followed 13 consecutive nights of bombing by the US, which said it had targeted Iranian weapons and military sites to diminish Iran's ability to attack commercial vessels attempting to transit the strait. Scores of people were reported to have died in the strikes.Iran responded to the US attacks by launching missiles and drones at US military assets in neighbouring Arab states. Four US service personnel were killed Jordan and Iraq.Access to and control of the Strait of Hormuz remain a key sticking point in negotiations between the US and Iran, which Iranian officials have denied are even happening.Oil prices rose early on Wednesday over concerns that an escalation in the conflict could further disrupt energy shipments through the strait, which has been effectively closed since the start of the US and Israel's war with Iran at the end of February.In morning trading in Asia, the global benchmark Brent crude was up by 4.3% to $87.70 (£65.98) a barrel, while US-traded oil was 4.2% higher at $82.62.The latest strikes coincided with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's visit to Washington, where he met Trump at the White House and attended the funeral of US Senator Lindsey Graham, a prominent Iran hawk.At least 624 US military service members have been wounded since Trump ordered strikes against Iran in February, according to recent Pentagon data.The Pentagon said 417 of those personnel were injured in relation to Operation Epic Fury, the joint US-Israeli military operation against Iran.
contentParagraphs.zh: 沙特阿拉伯和美国对伊拉克境内伊朗支持的民兵组织进行了打击，这可能导致中东冲突升级。美国中央司令部（Centcom）表示，此次袭击是针对“伊斯兰革命卫队（IRGC）指挥的与伊朗结盟的恐怖分子，目的是攻击美军和沙特能源基础设施”。以伊朗支持的什叶派民兵为主的伊拉克准军事民众动员部队（PMF）至少表示其 20 名成员在美国和沙特对其基地的袭击中丧生。数小时前，中央司令部表示，伊朗以“未遂的突然袭击”向中东美军发射了导弹，结束了敌对行动的平静。美国表示，伊朗的袭击发生在美国东部时间周二 17:45（格林尼治标准时间 21:45），所有导弹“被成功拦截”。伊朗革命卫队表示，这些导弹的目标是美国空军基地和一个指挥部。报告还称，海军部队在霍尔木兹海峡袭击了三艘油轮，因为这些油轮“无视警告”，并沿着所谓的“不安全和非法路线”穿越重要的海湾水道。中央司令部表示，美国和沙特战斗机袭击了“伊拉克东部多个恐怖分子后勤和武器基地，这是对伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队在伊拉克发动的 30 多次无人机袭击的强烈回应”。沙特国防部发言人图尔基·马利基少将还指责“伊朗支持的恐怖民兵”周一和周二从伊拉克领土向东部和利雅得地区的石油设施发射无人机。阿拉伯国家根据其“自卫权”，通过“针对这些民兵的特定目标”进行打击作为回应。他补充说：“沙特阿拉伯王国重申，它不寻求升级，但将对任何针对其的侵略做出果断反应。”PMF在周三上午的一份声明中表示，在美国和沙特对其位于沙特阿拉伯省份的一些总部的袭击中，至少有20名其战士被杀，另有32人受伤。巴格达、瓦西特、尼尼微、巴士拉、基尔库克、卡尔巴拉和迪亚拉。一名官员告诉法新社，北部尼尼微和中部迪亚拉的袭击是最致命的。PMF 谴责所谓的“背信弃义的恐怖袭击”，称这是“一次极其严重的升级，侵犯了伊拉克的主权，针对的是伊拉克官方安全机构”。PMF 是一个伞式组织，主要由什叶派穆斯林民兵已正式编入伊拉克武装部队。其中包括几个伊朗支持的组织，这些组织是德黑兰多年来用来推进其在中东地区利益的代理人网络的一部分。这些民兵多次袭击美国在伊拉克的人员和利益，旨在迫使剩余的美军离开该国。美国经常对民兵进行反击。据路透社报道，伊朗国家电视台援引伊朗国防官员的话说，否认伊朗与无人机袭击沙特阿拉伯有任何关系。该官员警告称，将美国在该地区利益受到的袭击归咎于伊朗是一个“重大误判”。美国和伊朗之间的敌对行动在唐纳德·特朗普总统谈到解决霍尔木兹海峡争端的“非常友好的谈判”两天后出现。当时，双方已连续三天没有交锋。美国连续13晚进行轰炸后，双方陷入了平静。美国称，它的目标是伊朗的武器和军事基地，以削弱伊朗攻击试图通过该海峡的商船的能力。据报道，数十人在袭击中死亡。伊朗对美国的袭击作出回应，向邻国阿拉伯国家的美国军事设施发射导弹和无人机。四名美国军人在约旦和伊拉克丧生。霍尔木兹海峡的进入和控制仍然是美国和伊朗之间谈判的一个关键症结，伊朗官员否认这种情况正在发生。周三早盘油价上涨，原因是担心冲突升级可能进一步扰乱通过该海峡的能源运输，自二月底美国和以色列与伊朗的战争开始以来，该海峡实际上已被关闭。亚洲早盘交易中，全球基准布伦特原油上涨每桶油价上涨 4.3% 至 87.70 美元（65.98 英镑），而美国交易的石油价格上涨 4.2% 至 82.62 美元。最近的袭击恰逢以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡访问华盛顿，他在白宫会见了特朗普，并参加了著名的伊朗鹰派美国参议员林赛·格雷厄姆的葬礼。据报道，自特朗普 2 月份下令对伊朗发动袭击以来，至少有 624 名美国军人受伤五角大楼最近的数据称，其中 417 名人员在美以针对伊朗的联合军事行动“史诗愤怒行动”中受伤。

articles.title: AI tool will lead to more child refugees being treated as adults, charity warns
articles.summary:
‘Racist bias’ overestimating ages in Home Office’s facial-recognition software will lead to solo children being housed with adults, says Human Rights Network
Flawed and racialised models that underpin the AI-powered age-detection systems to be introduced by the British government
articles.titleZh: 慈善机构警告人工智能工具将导致更多儿童难民被视为成年人
articles.summaryZh:
人权网络表示，内政部面部识别软件中高估年龄的“种族主义偏见”将导致独生儿童与成人同住
英国政府即将推出的人工智能年龄检测系统的基础是有缺陷和种族化的模型

contentParagraphs.en: Flawed and racialised models that underpin the AI-powered age-detection systems to be introduced by the British government will endanger children, rights groups and children’s charities have warned.Urging ministers to reverse plans to introduce facial age-estimation technology to screen migrants, critics have warned that black children arriving from conflict zones are at risk of being of thrust into the adult system.Maddie Harris, of the Humans for Rights Network, said the charity had worked with hundreds of children who were already being wrongly filtered into the adult system during age assessments at borders carried out by immigration officers.In May, the Helen Bamber Foundation revealed that 755 children in 2025 were incorrectly identified as adults on arrival to the UK, according to Home Office figures.Harris said the introduction of AI was a “cheap process” that would not improve these numbers. “This is not about protecting children – this is about shoring up the decisions that [the authorities] are making,” she said.The government has admitted that even the best systems can have a 30-month margin of error.Harris said this is particularly risky for children, especially those from countries such as Sudan and Somalia, who she said were already “adultified” by the system.“As soon as a child is treated as an adult, they are susceptible to – or exposed, rather – to any of the egregious consequences that the Home Office is applying to adults, such as detention and removal,” she said.Unaccompanied children would be forced into accommodation alongside adults, exposing them to risk and to the violence threatened by the rise in protests targeting accommodation for asylum seekers, she said.In May, the government announced a contract to use facial age-estimation technology developed by Cognitec, a German firm that calls itself “the face-recognition company”.That system showed bias against sub-Saharan Africans, tending to overpredict the ages of minors, according to an investigation by Lighthouse Reports in June.The UK-based tech monitor Foxglove has said these systems relied on “racist bias” and said the government should not use children to test experimental technology.The Refugee and Migrant Children’s Consortium has raised concerns about the technology’s ability to assess children who have undergone difficult journeys. It noted that trauma can “age” a child’s appearance.The Home Office plans to use the technology alongside checks by immigration officers. A spokesperson said: “Age assessments are a vital tool in maintaining border security. As part of our work to make this process more robust and consistent, we are exploring cutting-edge AI technology to verify migrants’ ages.”Petra Molnar, who co-founded the advocacy group Migration and Tech Monitor, said this was the latest in a series of failed attempts across Europe to implement tech and AI into border policy.She said previous attempts in Europe to implement AI-powered lie-detection systems for screening refugees had proven to be “snake oil” and did not progress beyond pilot schemes.She likened the use of facial age-estimation technology to “the study of skulls and skull shapes” by colonial-era scientists to categorise different ethnic groups, saying that like the discredited 19th-century pseudoscience of phrenology, these systems similarly relied on categorising physical features to determine age.“The context really matters here,” said Molnar. “We know that trauma ages you. We know that malnutrition, dehydration, torture – even just the journey itself – has physical impacts on your face, on your body.“It’s effectively ‘neo-phrenology’ by categorising people based on physical features,” she said. “Relying on these kind of imperfect tools is not the solution.”
contentParagraphs.zh: 英国政府即将推出的人工智能年龄检测系统的缺陷和种族化模型将危及儿童，权利组织和儿童慈善机构警告说。批评者敦促部长们扭转引入面部年龄估计技术来筛选移民的计划，批评者警告说，来自冲突地区的黑人儿童有被推入成人系统的风险。人权网络的麦迪·哈里斯表示，该慈善机构已与数百名已经被错误过滤到成人系统的儿童合作。移民官员在边境进行年龄评估时采用成人系统。今年 5 月，海伦·班伯基金会透露，根据内政部的数据，到 2025 年，将有 755 名儿童在抵达英国时被错误地识别为成年人。哈里斯表示，人工智能的引入是一个“廉价的过程”，不会改善这些数字。她说：“这不是为了保护儿童，而是为了支持（当局）正在做出的决定。”政府承认，即使是最好的系统也可能有 30 个月的误差范围。哈里斯说，这对儿童尤其危险，尤其是来自苏丹和索马里等国家的儿童，她说这些国家已经被该系统“成人化”了。她说，内政部对成年人适用的后果，例如拘留和驱逐。”她说，无人陪伴的儿童将被迫与成年人一起住在一起，使他们面临风险，并面临针对寻求庇护者住宿的抗议活动增加所带来的暴力威胁。5月，政府宣布了一份使用Cognitec公司开发的面部年龄估计技术的合同，Cognitec是一家自称为“人脸识别公司”的德国公司。该系统对撒哈拉以南非洲人表现出偏见，倾向于根据 Lighthouse Reports 6 月份的一项调查，高估了未成年人的年龄。总部位于英国的技术监测机构 Foxglove 表示，这些系统依赖于“种族主义偏见”，并表示政府不应使用儿童来测试实验技术。难民和移民儿童联盟对该技术评估经历过艰难旅程的儿童的能力表示担忧。报告指出，创伤会使孩子的外表“老化”。内政部计划在移民官员检查的同时使用该技术。一位发言人表示：“年龄评估是维护边境安全的重要工具。为了使这一过程更加稳健和一致，我们正在探索尖端人工智能技术来验证移民的年龄。”她将面部年龄估计技术的使用比作殖民时代科学家对不同种族群体进行分类的“头骨和头骨形状研究”，并表示，就像 19 世纪声名狼藉的颅相学伪科学一样，这些系统同样依赖于对身体特征进行分类来确定年龄。“这里的背景确实很重要，”莫尔纳说。 “我们知道创伤会让你变老。我们知道营养不良、脱水、折磨——甚至只是旅程本身——都会对你的脸、你的身体产生物理影响。“这实际上是根据身体特征对人进行分类的‘新颅相学’，”她说。“依赖这些不完美的工具并不是解决问题的办法。”

articles.title: 'Don't wait until you want revenge' - why prenups are on the rise
articles.summary: More young couples are now signing prenups to set out who gets what in the event of divorce.
articles.titleZh: “不要等到你想报复”——为什么婚前协议呈上升趋势
articles.summaryZh: 现在，越来越多的年轻夫妇签署婚前协议，规定离婚时谁能得到什么。

contentParagraphs.en: Celine Tsoi and Charles Mock met two years ago in Goleta, California when she was just 23 and he was 27. Eight months later they were engaged.Friends immediately asked: "Oh, are you getting a prenup?""A lot of things could happen in a marriage and you want to discuss them when you still love each other rather than when things go bad and you want to take revenge," says Celine.These days its not just the rich and famous; more of us are deciding it makes sense to have a legal agreement that sets out what happens to the money if the marriage ends, with younger couples particularly likely to sign one, even when there aren't great wealth differences to consider.Charles, a nurse, earns more than Celine does as a PhD student, but she had a bit more saved, so the disparities weren't big, but they wanted to face up to important financial questions from the start.She was particularly touched that Charles wanted the prenup to say if they split up, she should have the house.Just having the conversation "can show you what the person you're going to marry is like", she says.Becca expects to inherit a significant amount of property from her parents, which she wants to protect, so in the event of a split, each will walk away with what they started with."It's nice knowing that if anything were to happen, I would just go back to how life was before," she says.Dave, 45, admits it's unromantic but says, given the statistics around divorce, he wants to be pragmatic."A court of law could potentially say, hang on, this guy's earning a lot more than her, he needs to pay her."I built a home for myself. I've built a future for myself, including pensions."Park the emotional side of me loving both her and the kids, I'm no different now to when I met her, and yet she was independent. Why on earth would I have to pay something towards her life in the event of us splitting up?"Couples are also getting married later, points out Julia Rodgers, cofounder of US prenup platform HelloPrenup."You may have some [university] debt, maybe started a business or purchased a home. So you have a lot to protect and to lose by the age of 34," she says.What's become known as "the Great Wealth Transfer" means some members of the younger generation are receiving huge assets to manage. It is often their parents who are the driving force behind ring-fencing those inheritances.And while in the past prenups have been criticised for limiting women's rights, Rodgers argues they have evolved and now benefit women like her by giving them the chance to clarify their rights from the start."We want to make sure we have the honest, open, transparent conversations about life goals, about finances, about roles and responsibilities in the home, so that we can have a long, happy marriage and not end up in that position that we saw our parents in," she says.Celine says most of her friends think prenups are a good idea.It only cost her a few hundred dollars online, but even if she had had to pay lawyers it would have been a worthwhile "investment" in the marriage she says, and less expensive, but probably more important than the wedding itself.Best of all she and Charles have got the "hard conversations" out of the way."We haven't had a single argument about finances," she says.
contentParagraphs.zh: 两年前，席琳·蔡 (Celine Tsoi) 和查尔斯·莫克 (Charles Mock) 在加利福尼亚州戈利塔相识，当时她 23 岁，查尔斯·莫克 27 岁。八个月后，他们订婚了。朋友们立即问道：“哦，你们签婚前协议了吗？”席琳说：“婚姻中可能会发生很多事情，你想在仍然相爱的时候讨论这些事情，而不是在事情变坏而你想报复时讨论这些问题。”我们中越来越多的人认为，签订一份法律协议来规定婚姻结束后的钱的处理是有意义的，年轻夫妇特别有可能签署一份协议，即使没有考虑到巨大的财富差异。查尔斯是一名护士，比塞琳读博士时的收入高，但她的储蓄多一点，所以差距并不大，但他们想从一开始就面对重要的财务问题。她特别感动的是，查尔斯希望婚前协议说，如果他们分手，她她说，仅仅通过谈话“就能让你知道你要结婚的人是什么样的”。贝卡希望从父母那里继承大量财产，她想保护这些财产，所以如果离婚，双方都会带着最初的财产离开。“很高兴知道如果发生任何事情，我就会回到以前的生活，”她说。45 岁的戴夫承认这并不浪漫，但他说，考虑到统计数据在离婚问题上，他希望采取务实的态度。“法庭可能会说，等一下，这个人的收入比她多得多，他需要付钱给她。”我为自己建了一个家。我已经为自己建立了未来，包括养老金。“把我的情感方面放在爱她和孩子们身上，我现在和我遇见她时没有什么不同，但她是独立的。如果我们分手，我到底为什么要为她的生活付出一些代价？”美国婚前协议平台 HelloPrenup 联合创始人朱莉娅·罗杰斯指出，夫妻结婚的时间也越来越晚。所以到了 34 岁，你有很多东西需要保护，也有很多东西可以失去。”她说。所谓的“财富大转移”意味着年轻一代的一些成员正在接受巨额资产来管理。她们的父母往往是限制这些遗产的推动力。虽然过去婚前协议因限制女性权利而受到批评，但罗杰斯认为，婚前协议已经演变，现在让像她这样的女性有机会从一开始就澄清自己的权利，从而使她们受益。“我们希望确保我们就人生目标、财务、家庭角色和责任进行诚实、开放、透明的对话，这样我们才能拥有长久、幸福的婚姻，而不是最终陷入我们所看到的境地。”她说，“我们的父母都在。”席琳说，她的大多数朋友都认为婚前协议是个好主意。网上只花了她几百美元，但即使她必须付律师费，这对婚姻来说也是一笔值得的“投资”，而且成本更低，但可能比婚礼本身更重要。最重要的是，她和查尔斯已经摆脱了“艰难的对话”。“我们没有因为财务问题发生过任何争执，”她说。

articles.title: Tackling the 'nasty' plant that can cause blisters and scars
articles.summary: A conservation group says it has made progress tackling giant hogweed infestations in County Tyrone.
articles.titleZh: 解决可能引起水泡和疤痕的“讨厌”植物
articles.summaryZh: 一个保护组织表示，在解决蒂龙郡巨型猪草感染问题上已取得进展。

contentParagraphs.en: Tackling the 'nasty' plant that can cause blisters and scarsImage caption, Peter Mitchell from the Ballinderry Rivers Trust has been overseeing a project tackling giant hogweedByNiall McCrackenBBC News NI Mid Ulster ReporterA conservation project says it has been making progress tackling a plant which can cause painful blistering and scarring when its sap comes into contact with human skin.In the past, giant hogweed has been described as the UK's "most dangerous plant".The plant, which is an invasive species, can grow up to five metres high, and is usually found in places with damp soils, such as riverbanks and coastal areas.Peter Mitchell from The Ballinderry Rivers Trust describes it as: "A particularly nasty plant that you don't want to get close to."He says giant hogweed is also "fairly prominent" in Mid Ulster, and they have identified and begun treating a source of the plant just outside Cookstown, County Tyrone.Giant hogweed infestations in NIImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Giant hogweed should be avoided, experts warn (stock image)Mitchell says they have been concentrating on areas in and around Drum Manor Forest Park, close to the Ballinderry River."Thankfully we're now able to manage it keep it at an absolute minimum around Drum Manor, and that is a success story and we've been working successfully with local angling clubs to raise awareness."We've traced it to two water tributaries coming out of Drum Manor, so you can actually see the source of it coming in just above Cookstown, spreading down the Ballinderry River and as far as Lough Neagh.""Keeping on top of that is a monumental task," he adds.Image caption, Figures were provided by the NBN Atlas NI and NIEAThere are more than 2,500 sites across Northern Ireland, external where giant hogweed has been recorded and confirmed.Stormont has set a target for all landowners who have the plant on their land to reduce its distribution throughout Northern Ireland by 50% before 2030.Meanwhile new figures obtained by BBC News NI show there are more than 500 giant hogweed enforcement cases being pursued by the Northern Ireland Environment Agency.'I'll always remember the pain'Image caption, Sean Devlin has been fishing on the Ballinderry River for more than 60 yearsSean Devlin is a member of Mid Ulster Angling Club and has been fishing on the Ballinderry River for more than 60 years.He has firsthand experience of the effects of getting too close to giant hogweed."I'll never forget when I was a young lad, I was down at the riverbank and I got the plant all over my hands and arms, because I didn't know enough about the dangers at that time."I initially felt a small tingle, it wasn't like a nettle where you get the full sting immediately, it wasn't until later, especially when I was the sun with it that I really felt it on my skin."I ended up covered in these large watery blisters the whole way up my arm, I'll always remember the pain of it."He's urging anyone who sees it not to handle it and keep well away from it.'The pain was indescribable'Image source, Matt StoneImage caption, Esmée Gummer is a long distance runner who is currently taking on a 5,000km challenge across the UKEsmée Gummer is a long distance runner who is currently taking on a 5,000km challenge across the UK over a 99 day period.The English runner was once told she would never walk again after complications following surgery when she was 18 years old.She had to re-learn to walk and as part of her latest challenge is hosting a free 5k in every city she visits.Earlier this month while running in Northern Ireland she had to cope with blisters on her legs caused by exposure to giant hogweed in Scotland.She said: " I woke up one morning with these welts on my knees and I carried on running, I remember going to bed that night and woke up in agony.Image source, Matt StoneImage caption, Esmée Gummer was left with large blisters on her legs after coming into contact with the plant in Scotland "My knees were on fire and all these blisters began to form, I've never felt a pain like it."A doctor was able to bandage her legs, but she says "running through the pain was extremely tough"."I had really intense pain for about 10 days, particularly at night after running all day, the pain was indescribable, it was like fiery pain."Gummer says the support she received from people across Northern Ireland helped her run through the pain caused by the giant hogweed burns.What is giant hogweed?Image caption, A sign warning about the dangers of Giant Hogweed at Ballyronan Marina Giant hogweed is a toxic plant, which originates from Asia, but has been present in Britain and Ireland since the early 19th Century.It was first introduced as an ornamental garden plant used primarily in large stately homes, but it subsequently escaped into the wider countryside.The plant, which can grow up to 14-15ft (4.5m) tall, is now associated with river corridors and lake margins in all counties of Northern Ireland.It contains a sap which irritates skin when it is exposed to sunlight and can cause blistering and swelling.Symptoms are usually noticeable within 24 hours and may be made worse by over-exposure to the sun.Government advice around contact with giant hogweed is to cover any affected skin immediately, wash with cold water and avoid exposure in the sun.The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) advises anyone who is concerned about giant hogweed to report it through its official monitoring system or the apps iRecord or iNaturalist.A spokesperson for NIEA said: "Each record is followed up, with landowners being informed of their legal responsibilities to put immediate management measures in place."
contentParagraphs.zh: 解决这种会引起水泡和疤痕的“讨厌”植物 图片说明，来自巴林德里河信托基金的彼得·米切尔一直在监督一个处理巨型猪草的项目 作者：尼尔·麦克拉肯 BBC 新闻 NI 阿尔斯特中部记者 一个保护项目表示，它在处理一种植物方面取得了进展，这种植物的汁液与人类皮肤接触时会引起痛苦的水泡和疤痕。过去，巨型猪草被描述为英国的“最危险的植物”。这种植物是一种入侵物种，可以长到五米高，通常出现在土壤潮湿的地方，例如河岸和沿海地区。巴林德里河流信托基金会的彼得·米切尔将其描述为：“一种你不想靠近的特别令人讨厌的植物。”他说，巨猪草在阿尔斯特中部也“相当突出”，他们已经在库克斯敦郊外发现并开始处理该植物的来源，蒂龙县。 NI 的巨型猪草感染 图片来源，盖蒂图片社 图片说明，专家警告说，应该避免巨型猪草（库存图片）米切尔说，他们一直把重点放在 Drum Manor 森林公园及其周围地区，靠近巴林德里河。 “我们已经追踪到它来自 Drum Manor 的两条水支流，所以你实际上可以看到它的源头就在库克斯敦上方，沿着巴林德里河一直延伸到内湖。”他补充道，“保持这一点是一项艰巨的任务。”他补充道。图片说明，数据由 NBN Atlas NI 和 NIEA 提供。北爱尔兰各地有 2,500 多个地点，外部是巨型猪草生长的地方。斯托蒙特为所有在其土地上拥有该植物的土地所有者设定了一个目标，即在 2030 年之前将其在整个北爱尔兰的分布减少 50%。与此同时，英国广播公司新闻 NI 获得的新数据显示，北爱尔兰环境局正在追查 500 多起巨型猪草执法案件。“我将永远记住这种痛苦”图片说明，肖恩·德夫林 (Sean Devlin) 60 多年来一直在巴林德里河 (Ballinderry River) 钓鱼 肖恩·德夫林 (Sean Devlin)阿尔斯特中部钓鱼俱乐部的成员，在巴林德里河上钓鱼已有 60 多年。他对离巨型猪草太近的影响有亲身体验。“我永远不会忘记，当我还是个小伙子时，我在河岸边，我的手和手臂上都沾满了这种植物，因为当时我对其中的危险了解不够。”我最初感到一种轻微的刺痛感，它不像荨麻，你会在河边遇到这种植物。立即完全刺痛，直到后来，特别是当我在阳光下时，我才真正感觉到它在我的皮肤上。“我的手臂上一直覆盖着这些大水泡，我会永远记住它的痛苦。”他敦促任何看到它的人不要处理它并远离它。穿越英国的 5,000 公里挑战 埃斯米·古默 (Esmée Gummer) 是一名长跑运动员，目前正在英国接受为期 99 天的 5,000 公里挑战。这位英国跑步运动员曾在 18 岁时因手术并发症而被告知她再也不能走路了。她必须重新学习走路，作为她最新挑战的一部分，她将在她访问的每个城市举办免费 5 公里赛。本月早些时候，她在北爱尔兰跑步时她说：“有一天早上，我醒来时膝盖上有这些伤痕，但我继续跑步，我记得那天晚上上床睡觉时，我在痛苦中醒来。图片来源，马特·斯通图片说明，埃斯米·古默在苏格兰接触到这种植物后，腿上留下了大水泡。“我的膝盖着火了，所有这些水泡都开始形成，我从来没有感觉到医生帮她包扎了双腿，但她说“忍受疼痛跑步非常艰难”。“我有大约十天的时间感到非常剧烈的疼痛，特别是在跑了一整天后的晚上，这种疼痛是难以形容的，就像火烧般的疼痛。”古默说，北爱尔兰各地人们的支持帮助她克服了巨型猪草烧伤造成的痛苦。什么是巨型猪草？图片说明，一个警告巨型猪草危险的标志巴利罗南码头的大猪草 巨型大猪草是一种有毒植物，原产于亚洲，但自 19 世纪初期以来就出现在英国和爱尔兰。它最初是作为观赏花园植物引入的，主要用于大型豪宅，但随后逃逸到更广阔的乡村。这种植物可长到 14-15 英尺（4.5 m）高，现在与北爱尔兰所有县的河流走廊和湖泊边缘都有联系。它包含汁液暴露在阳光下会刺激皮肤，并可能导致起泡和肿胀。症状通常会在 24 小时内显现出来，过度暴露在阳光下可能会变得更严重。政府关于接触大猪草的建议是立即覆盖受影响的皮肤，用冷水清洗并避免暴露在阳光下。北爱尔兰环境局 (NIEA) 建议任何担心大猪草的人通过其官方监控系统或应用程序报告此事iRecord 或 iNaturalist。NIEA 的一位发言人表示：“每条记录都会得到跟进，土地所有者会被告知他们的法律责任，以立即采取管理措施。”

articles.title: New York school pauses plan to deploy humanlike AI robot teacher after backlash
articles.summary: A school district in upstate New York is pausing plans to deploy an AI-powered, humanoid robot in the classroom after state education officials, teachers and local residents raised concerns.
articles.titleZh: 纽约学校因强烈反对而暂停部署类人人工智能机器人教师的计划
articles.summaryZh: 在州教育官员、教师和当地居民提出担忧后，纽约州北部的一个学区暂停了在教室部署人工智能人形机器人的计划。

contentParagraphs.en: FILE - A Realbotix humanoid robot, center, speaks with attendees at a Realbotix booth during the CES tech show Jan. 8, 2025, in Las Vegas.
contentParagraphs.zh: 文件 - 2025 年 1 月 8 日在拉斯维加斯举行的 CES 科技展期间，Realbotix 人形机器人（中）在 Realbotix 展位上与与会者交谈。

contentParagraphs.en: NEW YORK — A school district in a rural corner of upstate New York is hitting pause on plans to deploy an AI-powered, humanoid robot in the classroom after state education officials, teachers and local residents raised concerns, including the maker's ties to a company that produces hyper realistic sex bots.
contentParagraphs.zh: 纽约——纽约州北部农村一角的一个学区暂停了在课堂上部署人工智能人形机器人的计划，此前州教育官员、教师和当地居民提出了担忧，其中包括该学区与一家生产超现实性爱机器人的公司的关系。

contentParagraphs.en: The Salamanca City Central School District's board approved the nearly $60,000 purchase from Realbotix with visions that "Sally," as the stationary robot with long dark hair has already been nicknamed, would enhance the education of high school students studying robotics and technology fields.
contentParagraphs.zh: 萨拉曼卡市中央学区董事会批准了从 Realbotix 购买近 60,000 美元的资金，其愿景是“莎莉”（这个长着黑长发的固定机器人的昵称）将加强对学习机器人和技术领域的高中生的教育。

contentParagraphs.en: "Having a difficult time programming an Arduino board? Don't even know what an Arduino board is? Ask Sally and she can explain it," Superintendent Mark Beehler, said Tuesday. "The robot also provides opportunities for students to learn how the robot is maintained, how it is updated with new approved content, and how to troubleshoot issues."
contentParagraphs.zh: “对 Arduino 板进行编程时遇到困难？甚至不知道 Arduino 板是什么？问问 Sally，她可以解释它，”警司 Mark Beehler 周二表示。 “该机器人还为学生提供了学习如何维护机器人、如何使用新批准的内容进行更新以及如何解决问题的机会。”

contentParagraphs.en: But as news spread in the small community located on the Seneca Nation of Indians reservation, parents and teachers worried about how students' personal information would be used. Unionized teachers took aim at Realbotix's sex doll sister company, even as district officials and the company itself stressed the two manufacturers operate independently.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但随着消息在塞内卡印第安人保留地的小社区传播开来，家长和老师担心学生的个人信息将被如何使用。工会教师将矛头指向了 Realbotix 的性玩偶姐妹公司，尽管地区官员和该公司本身都强调这两家制造商是独立运营的。

contentParagraphs.en: "A robot built by a company associated with sex dolls has no business in our classrooms," said Melinda Person, president of the labor union New York State United Teachers.
contentParagraphs.zh: 纽约州联合教师工会主席梅琳达·珀森表示：“与性玩偶相关的公司制造的机器人不适合我们的教室。”

contentParagraphs.en: For now, the robot pilot remains on hold as the district works through "enhanced student data privacy agreements" with the state education officials and continues outreach to the community, according to a statement the district posted Friday on its Facebook page.
contentParagraphs.zh: 根据该学区周五在其 Facebook 页面上发布的一份声明，目前，机器人飞行员仍处于搁置状态，因为该学区正在与州教育官员签订“增强型学生数据隐私协议”，并继续向社区进行推广。

contentParagraphs.en: State officials and teacher voice concerns
contentParagraphs.zh: 州政府官员和教师表达了担忧

contentParagraphs.en: State Education Commissioner Betty Rosa said she remained concerned about the robot's role in the classroom even after her staff met with district officials.
contentParagraphs.zh: 州教育专员贝蒂·罗莎表示，即使她的工作人员与地区官员会面后，她仍然对机器人在课堂上的作用感到担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: "Although you confirmed that the robot would not have any role delivering classroom instruction, a recent presentation to the board characterized the robot as a 'tutoring platform,' " Rosa wrote in a letter to the district Friday.
contentParagraphs.zh: 罗莎周五在给学区的一封信中写道：“尽管你们确认机器人不会在课堂教学中发挥任何作用，但最近向董事会提交的一份报告将机器人描述为‘辅导平台’。”

contentParagraphs.en: She also echoed residents' concerns about what data privacy and security protections would be in place.
contentParagraphs.zh: 她还回应了居民对数据隐私和安全保护措施的担忧。

contentParagraphs.en: Unionized teachers, meanwhile, suggested the effort was a first step toward replacing, flesh-and-bone educators. "Sally" will be able to move her arms and hands but have nonworking legs.
contentParagraphs.zh: 与此同时，工会教师表示，此举是更换有血有肉的教育工作者的第一步。 “莎莉”将能够移动她的手臂和手，但双腿不能活动。

contentParagraphs.en: "Our students don't need robots," Person said. "They need real relationships with caring adults."
contentParagraphs.zh: “我们的学生不需要机器人，”珀森说。 “他们需要与有爱心的成年人建立真正的关系。”

contentParagraphs.en: District officials defend robot purchase
contentParagraphs.zh: 地区官员为机器人购买辩护

contentParagraphs.en: Beehler stressed the pilot, which also includes rollout of a virtual, AI-powered teacher's assistant and at-home tutoring program, is not about replacing staff.
contentParagraphs.zh: 比勒强调，该试点项目还包括推出由人工智能驱动的虚拟教师助理和家庭辅导计划，并不是为了更换员工。

contentParagraphs.en: "There is no possible way a robot can replace a human in a school," he said Tuesday. "Even if it were possible, it would in no way be in the best interest of students. Teaching is a human-to-human process."
contentParagraphs.zh: “机器人不可能在学校里取代人类，”他周二表示。 “即使有可能，也绝不符合学生的最大利益。教学是一个人与人之间的过程。”

contentParagraphs.en: Beehler, who was connected to Realbotix through a former colleague, said the Las Vegas-based company was a natural fit because its robots are already programmed with WozEd, a curriculum from Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak that the district uses.
contentParagraphs.zh: Beehler 通过一位前同事与 Realbotix 建立了联系，他表示这家总部位于拉斯维加斯的公司非常适合，因为它的机器人已经使用 WozEd 进行了编程，WozEd 是该地区使用的苹果联合创始人史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克 (Steve Wozniak) 的课程。

contentParagraphs.en: Last year, a San Diego charter school rolled out two AI-powered robots purchased from Engineered Arts, a robotics company based in the United Kingdom, for $500,000.
contentParagraphs.zh: 去年，圣地亚哥一所特许学校推出了两台人工智能机器人，这些机器人是从英国机器人公司 Engineered Arts 购买的，价格为 50 万美元。

contentParagraphs.en: Salamanca Schools, in social media posts, stressed that "Sally" won't be collecting students' personal information, recording audio or video of its interactions or sending data back to Realbotix.
contentParagraphs.zh: 萨拉曼卡学校在社交媒体帖子中强调，“Sally”不会收集学生的个人信息、录制其互动的音频或视频或将数据发送回 Realbotix。

contentParagraphs.en: The robot also has been programmed to steer clear of inappropriate topics such as sex, violence and gambling, and it won't be able to search the public internet or draw answers from unvetted generative AI services.
contentParagraphs.zh: 该机器人还被编程为避开性、暴力和赌博等不恰当的话题，它无法搜索公共互联网或从未经审查的生成人工智能服务中得出答案。

contentParagraphs.en: Instead, all information on "Sally" will be stored locally, with the life-sized robot consuming roughly the same amount of energy as a laptop, according to the district.
contentParagraphs.zh: 相反，有关“莎莉”的所有信息都将存储在本地，根据该地区的说法，真人大小的机器人消耗的能量与笔记本电脑大致相同。

contentParagraphs.en: Robot maker responds to criticism
contentParagraphs.zh: 机器人制造商回应批评

contentParagraphs.en: Realbotix added Tuesday that student authentication would be handled through the district's existing systems, and any student-linked information would remain encrypted and under the district's control.
contentParagraphs.zh: Realbotix 周二补充说，学生身份验证将通过学区现有系统进行处理，任何与学生相关的信息都将保持加密状态并处于学区的控制之下。

contentParagraphs.en: The company also pushed back at suggestions that "Sally" was simply a repurposed sex doll, saying it was a "newly manufactured, purpose-built educational unit" with no modified hardware.
contentParagraphs.zh: 该公司还反驳了“莎莉”只是一个重新设计的性玩偶的说法，称它是一个“新制造的、专门建造的教育装置”，没有修改硬件。

contentParagraphs.en: The school's robot comes from Realbotix LLC, which focuses on healthcare, education and other nonadult commercial applications. A sister company, Intima LLC, holds an ownership stake in RealDoll, a longtime maker of sex dolls, including a line of AI-powered models billed as the "world's most advanced sex robot."
contentParagraphs.zh: 该学校的机器人来自Realbotix LLC，专注于医疗保健、教育和其他非成人商业应用。姊妹公司 Intima LLC 持有 RealDoll 的所有权股份，RealDoll 是一家长期生产性玩偶的制造商，其中包括一系列被称为“世界上最先进的性爱机器人”的人工智能模型。

contentParagraphs.en: "Realbotix LLC and Intima LLC have different product offerings with no crossover," the company said in a statement last week. "The two subsidiaries maintain their own management, personnel, payroll, facilities, manufacturing operations, product development, and market strategies."
contentParagraphs.zh: “Realbotix LLC 和 Intima LLC 提供不同的产品，没有交叉，”该公司上周在一份声明中表示。 “这两家子公司保持自己的管理、人员、工资、设施、制造业务、产品开发和市场战略。”

contentParagraphs.en: Some residents remain wary
contentParagraphs.zh: 部分居民仍保持警惕

contentParagraphs.en: Beehler argued that it is crucial for isolated districts like Salamanca, which is located along the Allegheny River near the Pennsylvania state line, to find new ways to introduce cutting-edge products into classrooms.
contentParagraphs.zh: 比勒认为，对于像萨拉曼卡这样位于宾夕法尼亚州线附近阿勒格尼河沿岸的偏远地区来说，找到将尖端产品引入课堂的新方法至关重要。

contentParagraphs.en: "In most cases, our students need to travel 1-2 hours to have opportunities to see emergent technology," he said Tuesday. "One of the intents of the robot is to help level the playing field and motivate students to continue studying robotics, AI, and STEAM related career pathways."
contentParagraphs.zh: “在大多数情况下，我们的学生需要花 1 到 2 小时才能有机会看到新兴技术，”他周二表示。 “该机器人的目的之一是帮助创造公平的竞争环境并激励学生继续学习机器人技术、人工智能和 STEAM 相关的职业道路。”

contentParagraphs.en: Some Salamanca residents, though, remain unconvinced.
contentParagraphs.zh: 不过，一些萨拉曼卡居民仍然不相信。

contentParagraphs.en: Joplin Ficek, who graduated from Salamanca High School in 2024 and now works at a daycare, said she doesn't see any reason to have robots or AI take such a prominent role at her alma mater at all.
contentParagraphs.zh: 乔普林·菲塞克 (Joplin Ficek) 于 2024 年从萨拉曼卡高中毕业，现在在一家日托中心工作，她表示，她认为机器人或人工智能根本没有任何理由在她的母校扮演如此重要的角色。

articles.title: US bans humanoid robots from China, citing ‘unacceptable risks’
articles.summary:
Move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US
The Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on humanoid robots from China on Tuesday, saying that the technology poses “unacceptable risks” to the country’s national
articles.titleZh: 美国以“不可接受的风险”为由禁止中国人形机器人
articles.summaryZh:
此举之际，特朗普政府越来越多地寻求将中国技术拒之门外
美国联邦通信委员会周二宣布禁止来自中国的人形机器人，称该技术对中国国家安全构成“不可接受的风险”

contentParagraphs.en: The Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on humanoid robots from China on Tuesday, saying that the technology poses “unacceptable risks” to the country’s national security. The move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US.The FCC defines the banned robots as “advanced robotic devices”, which include humanoids and animal-like quadrupeds.“Advanced robotic devices collect data that could be leveraged by malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots,” FCC officials wrote in their determination of the threat posed by robots.In addition to the humanoid robots, the FCC also barred connected power inverters, which enable renewable energy sources and batteries to connect to grids and datacenter equipment.The restrictions point to the Trump administration’s goal of elevating technology made in the US, along with driving firms to shift manufacturing to be done locally.“The president has made clear that the United States must have independent and secure supply chains for critical and emerging technologies like robotic devices and power inverters,” an ⁠administration official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.“Economic security is national security, and the Trump administration continues to implement a nuanced and multi-faceted policy agenda to reindustrialize America,” he added.China’s embassy in Washington said Beijing “urges the United ⁠States to heed the objective and rational voices of the business communities in both countries” and “stop smearing Chinese companies and threatening them with sanctions”.China’s government will “take all necessary measures in response to any action that causes material ​harm to its interests,” the embassy said.Chinese newspaper the Global Times quoted Xiang Ligang, from the Zhongguancun Information Consumption Alliance, as saying: “The series of moves by the United States reflects a deep sense of anxiety.“The US knows that its former technological advantage is rapidly eroding, but remains determined to preserve its position as the world’s leading technological power. It has abandoned rational calculation, lashed out indiscriminately and introduced a range of irrational restrictions.”The restrictions apply only to robot and inverter models that have not yet been released. However, the FCC has the authority to ‌revoke authorizations for sales of models that have already been authorized for purchase in the US.Humanoid robots, topped with ‌AI-enabled “brains”, are forecast by some analysts for broad adoption in ‌consumer and industrial arenas, while explosive datacenter construction in the US will depend on reliable sources of inverters.China is the world’s largest maker of inverters, led by Sungrow Power Supply and Huawei, which are already heavily sanctioned by the US.
contentParagraphs.zh: 美国联邦通信委员会周二宣布禁止来自中国的人形机器人，称该技术对国家安全构成“不可接受的风险”。此举出台之际，特朗普政府越来越力图将中国技术排除在美国之外。FCC 将被禁止的机器人定义为“先进机器人设备”，其中包括类人机器人和类似动物的四足动物。FCC 官员在确定机器人构成的威胁时写道，“先进机器人设备收集的数据可能被恶意行为者用来监视美国人、增强外国情报部门的能力或远程征用机器人。”还禁止联网逆变器，这些逆变器使可再生能源和电池能够连接到电网和数据中心设备。这些限制表明特朗普政府的目标是提升美国制造的技术，同时推动企业将制造转移到本地。一位不愿透露姓名的政府官员告诉路透社：“总统已明确表示，美国必须为机器人设备和逆变器等关键和新兴技术拥有独立且安全的供应链。”“经济安全就是国家安全，特朗普政府他补充说，中国驻华盛顿大使馆表示，北京“敦促美国倾听两国工商界客观理性的声音”，“停止抹黑中国企业并以制裁相威胁”。中国政府将“采取一切必要措施，应对任何对其利益造成实质损害的行为”。中国报纸《环球时报》援引中关村信息消费联盟项立刚表示：“美国的一系列举动，反映出一种深深的焦虑感。”它放弃了理性计算，肆意抨击，并引入了一系列不合理的限制。“这些限制仅适用于尚未发布的机器人和逆变器型号。然而，FCC有权撤销已在美国授权购买的型号的销售授权。一些分析师预测，搭载人工智能“大脑”的人形机器人将在消费和工业领域广泛采用，同时数据中心建设将呈爆炸式增长。美国将依赖可靠的逆变器来源。中国是全球最大的逆变器制造商，以阳光电源和华为为首，这两家公司已经受到美国的严厉制裁。

articles.title: As many are priced out of buying, the renter-owner wealth gap is wider than ever
articles.summary: Record high housing costs have pushed the wealth gap between renters and owners wider than ever. It's been a boon for owners even as many others are priced out.
articles.titleZh: 由于许多人因价格过高而放弃购买，租户与业主的贫富差距比以往任何时候都更大

contentParagraphs.en: SACHA PFEIFFER, HOST: This summer, the median U.S. home price hit another record high - $444,000. That yearslong upward trend has widened the wealth gap between renters and owners more than ever. That's been a boon for owners, but it's pricing out many would-be buyers, as NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports.JENNIFER LUDDEN, BYLINE: Jay Washington is 38 and grew up in the house his mother bought in Augusta, Georgia. She had no college degree and used only her single income at a local manufacturing plant.JAY WASHINGTON: The real estate agent told her in about, like, five years (laughter) you're probably going to give me a call and, like, thank me for being able to get this house.LUDDEN: And she did. Today, she's still there, and the home's value has grown to nearly $300,000. Washington lives a couple hours away in Athens and would love to own a home, not only for financial security.WASHINGTON: It is really kind of a sign that you truly feel independent.LUDDEN: But like so many millennials, he graduated college at the height of the great recession, with unemployment peaking at 10%. What's more, his degree from a for-profit college - later sued for alleged deception - seemed worthless.WASHINGTON: I basically was stuck in a cycle of, like, unemployment or underemployment.LUDDEN: Washington eventually got another college degree and now has a good job in IT. But with student loans, plus the high cost of rent, food and so much else, it's hard to save for a down payment. Meantime, home prices have surged more than 50% in just the last six years.WASHINGTON: I feel like I'm just kind of, like, surviving. At this point, I'm not really sure if I'm going to be able to own a house.MECHELE DICKERSON: Most middle-class families have most of their wealth in their homes.LUDDEN: Mechele Dickerson researches housing and the middle class at the University of Texas at Austin. She worries about the long-term consequences as more people are shut out of ownership.DICKERSON: For young adults who are middle class, they are facing a future of no wealth.LUDDEN: To be clear, she says there's nothing wrong with renting if you can still save for retirement. It might work better for some. But for generations, it's been housing wealth that has helped many do better than their parents.DICKERSON: We're ending up in this space where if you're OK, it may be because your parents were OK. And if your parents were struggling, you may be struggling, too.(SOUNDBITE OF DOOR KNOCKING)BRITTANY GILROY: Hi.LUDDEN: Hi.GILROY: This is Basil. He just...LUDDEN: Hello.GILROY: ...Wants to sniff you.LUDDEN: In Richmond, Virginia, Brittany Gilroy and her husband, Phillip West, rent this red brick, two-story home along with a roommate. Both are 35, and when they moved in with a friend, they thought it would be only for a few months until they bought a house. That was nearly four years ago.GILROY: Pretty much every time, when we looked at a house, we went, ugh. We said no. And then the prices of the houses go up.LUDDEN: Both of them have good-paying jobs, but the homes they see are either way above their price range or need repairs that would wipe them out. It's all put on hold another major life decision.PHILLIP WEST: It's definitely part of our consideration for, do we have kids or not, you know (laughter)? And it's a bit of a clock.LUDDEN: Gilroy only wants children if they can buy a place and settle down - safe neighborhood, good schools. But with prices so high, they worry about taking on all that debt.GILROY: I feel like we're not the only ones living in this constant state of uncertainty, and if you want to make a dive into buying a house, you're going into the deep end. There is no kiddie pool of a starter home.LUDDEN: In fact, there is a massive housing shortage, especially of starter homes, and it's driving prices up. Last year, a housing developer in Utah urged the state to make it easier to build affordable condos. And in that letter, he warned about the widening wealth gap between owners and renters. Tom Henriod of Rockworth Companies wrote that it could foster, quote, "discord between classes and increased risk of societal unrest."TOM HENRIOD: That might be going to a little bit of an extreme, but if there's a feeling that there's a few haves and a bunch of have-nots, I think all of us can see some of the problems that come with that.LUDDEN: He also has four children and says young people need hope that they can make it on their own.HENRIOD: You see how much a house might cost that you might want to live in, and you look at your income coming out of college or something like that, it might feel overwhelming, depressing, you know, difficult and that's certainly an effect, for sure.LUDDEN: Congress recently weighed in with a law that aims to eventually expand the supply of homes. And prices in some places are cooling off. contentParagraphs.zh: 主持人 SACHA PFEIFFER：今年夏天，美国房价中位数再创历史新高 - 444,000 美元。长达数年的上升趋势使租房者和业主之间的贫富差距比以往任何时候都更大。正如 NPR 的詹妮弗·卢登 (Jennifer Ludden) 报道的那样，这对业主来说是一个福音，但它却让许多潜在买家望而却步。詹妮弗·卢登连线：杰伊·华盛顿 (Jay Washington) 38 岁，在他母亲在佐治亚州奥古斯塔购买的房子里长大。她没有大学学位，只用自己在当地一家制造厂的单一收入。 杰伊·华盛顿： 房地产经纪人告诉她，大约五年后（笑声），你可能会给我打电话，感谢我能够得到这栋房子。 鲁登： 她做到了。如今，她仍然在那里，房子的价值已经增长到近 30 万美元。华盛顿住在距离雅典几个小时路程的地方，他很想拥有一套房子，不仅仅是为了经济保障。华盛顿：这确实是一个迹象，表明你真正感到独立。卢登：但像许多千禧一代一样，他在经济大衰退最严重的时候大学毕业，失业率达到 10% 的峰值。更重要的是，他从一所营利性大学获得的学位 - 后来因涉嫌欺骗而被起诉 - 似乎毫无价值。 华盛顿：我基本上陷入了失业或就业不足的循环。 鲁登：华盛顿最终获得了另一个大学学位，现在在 IT 领域找到了一份好工作。但由于学生贷款，再加上高昂的房租、食品和其他费用，很难存够首付。与此同时，房价在过去六年里飙升了 50% 以上。 华盛顿：我觉得我只是勉强生存而已。在这一点上，我不太确定我是否能够拥有一套房子。 MECHELE DICKERSON：大多数中产阶级家庭的大部分财富都在他们的房子里。LUDDEN：Mechele Dickerson 在德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校研究住房和中产阶级。她担心越来越多的人被排除在所有权之外而带来的长期后果。 迪克森：对于中产阶级的年轻人来说，他们面临着没有财富的未来。 鲁登：需要明确的是，她说，如果你仍然可以为退休储蓄，那么租房并没有什么问题。对某些人来说可能效果更好。但对于几代人来说，住房财富帮助许多人比他们的父母做得更好。 迪克森：我们最终会陷入这样的境地：如果你还好，那可能是因为你的父母还好。如果你的父母正在苦苦挣扎，你也可能正在苦苦挣扎。（敲门声）布列塔尼·吉尔罗伊：嗨。鲁登：嗨。吉尔罗伊：我是巴兹尔。他只是... 卢登：你好。吉尔罗伊：...想闻你。卢登：在弗吉尼亚州里士满，布列塔尼·吉尔罗伊和她的丈夫菲利普·韦斯特与室友一起租了这座红砖两层楼的房子。两人都 35 岁了，当他们搬去和朋友住在一起时，他们以为只需要几个月就能买房。那是差不多四年前的事了。 吉尔罗伊：几乎每次，当我们看房子时，我们都会说，呃。我们说不。然后房子的价格就会上涨。 鲁登：他们都有高薪工作，但他们看到的房子要么远远超出他们的价格范围，要么需要修理，这会让他们破产。这一切都被搁置了另一个重大的人生决定。 PHILLIP WEST：这绝对是我们考虑的一部分，我们是否有孩子，你知道吗（笑声）？卢登：吉尔罗伊只想要孩子，前提是他们能买房并安定下来——安全的社区、好的学校。但由于房价如此之高，他们担心承担所有债务。 吉尔罗伊：我觉得我们并不是唯一生活在这种持续的不确定状态中的人，如果你想一头扎进买房，你就会陷入困境。没有适合儿童的入门房。卢登：事实上，住房严重短缺，尤其是入门房，这导致价格上涨。去年，犹他州的一位住房开发商敦促该州让建造经济适用公寓变得更加容易。在那封信中，他警告业主和租户之间不断扩大的贫富差距。罗克沃斯公司的汤姆·亨里奥德写道，它可能会助长“阶级之间的不和，增加社会动荡的风险。” 汤姆·亨里奥德：这可能有点极端，但如果有一种感觉，有一些富人和一群穷人，我想我们所有人都能看到随之而来的一些问题。 鲁登：他还有四个孩子，并说年轻人需要希望他们能够靠自己的努力取得成功。亨里欧德：你看看你想要住的房子可能要花多少钱，你看看你大学毕业或类似的收入，这可能会让人感到不知所措、沮丧，你知道，困难，这肯定是一种影响。 卢登：国会最近权衡了一项旨在最终扩大住房供应的法律。一些地方的价格正在降温。不过，就目前而言，在区分住房富人和穷人的众多因素中，一个重要因素是时机。 马特·马拉塞克：那是我大学四年级，有一栋止赎房屋。 鲁登：马特·马拉塞克在 2010 年与一位朋友使用房地产崩溃后建立的联邦税收抵免政策购买了他的第一套房子。他们在地下室增加了卧室并将其出租。不久之后，他的女朋友（现在的妻子）阿曼达只花了 5,000 美元首付买了一套小型的待修房屋。阿曼达：非常非常过时。浴室里铺着地毯，有呕吐绿色的水槽和与之相配的呕吐绿色的烤箱。 卢登：家人一起努力把它打扮得漂漂亮亮的。几年后，他们震惊地发现，

articles.title: Rand Paul releases Anthony Fauci's pandemic-era diary notes. Here's what they tell us
articles.summary: Sen. Rand Paul has released a tranche of Dr. Anthony Fauci's diary entries from the COVID-19 pandemic. Fauci is set to appear before a Senate committee Wednesday on the origins of the coronavirus.
articles.titleZh: 兰德·保罗发布了安东尼·福奇大流行时期的日记。这是他们告诉我们的
articles.summaryZh: 参议员兰德·保罗 (Rand Paul) 发布了安东尼·福奇博士 (Anthony Fauci) 的一部分关于 COVID-19 大流行的日记。福奇将于周三就冠状病毒的起源问题出席参议院委员会。

contentParagraphs.en: Dr. Anthony Fauci testifies before the House Oversight and Accountability Committee Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus Pandemic on June 3, 2024, in Washington, D.C. Fauci is expected to appear before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Wednesday.
contentParagraphs.zh: 安东尼·福奇博士将于 2024 年 6 月 3 日在华盛顿特区的众议院监督和问责委员会冠状病毒大流行特别小组委员会作证。福奇预计将于周三在参议院国土安全和政府事务委员会作证。

contentParagraphs.en: Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., published a tranche of diary entries over the weekend made by Dr. Anthony Fauci during the COVID-19 pandemic. The release of the 1,141-page document came ahead of Fauci's appearance before a Senate committee on Wednesday.
contentParagraphs.zh: 肯塔基州共和党参议员兰德·保罗 (Rand Paul) 发表了安东尼·福奇 (Anthony Fauci) 博士周末在 COVID-19 大流行期间撰写的一系列日记。这份长达 1,141 页的文件是在福奇周三出席参议院委员会会议之前发布的。

contentParagraphs.en: The entries, and Paul's commentary on them, highlight the disagreement between the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and some politicians over the origins of the coronavirus.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这些条目以及保罗对它们的评论凸显了美国国家过敏和传染病研究所 (NIAID) 前所长与一些政界人士在冠状病毒起源问题上的分歧。

contentParagraphs.en: Paul and Fauci — who served as a key member of the White House's Coronavirus Task Force — have disagreed publicly for years over how the pandemic began. Even after Fauci stepped down from his position at NIAID at the end of 2022, Paul has continued to conduct an "investigation into the origins of COVID-19 and risky taxpayer-funded life sciences research."
contentParagraphs.zh: 保罗和曾担任白宫冠状病毒特别工作组主要成员的福奇多年来一直在大流行如何开始的问题上公开存在分歧。即使 Fauci 于 2022 年底辞去 NIAID 职务后，Paul 仍继续进行“对 COVID-19 的起源和纳税人资助的有风险的生命科学研究的调查”。

contentParagraphs.en: On Saturday afternoon, as part of this ongoing inquiry, Paul published a thread on X describing the release of a string of what he called diary entries made by Fauci from December 2019 through December 2022. Paul commented on X at the start of the posts, "What [Fauci] wrote privately and what he told the country are two different stories."
contentParagraphs.zh: 周六下午，作为正在进行的调查的一部分，保罗在 X 上发布了一条帖子，描述了福奇从 2019 年 12 月到 2022 年 12 月期间所写的一系列日记的发布。保罗在帖子开头对 X 发表了评论，“[福奇]私下写的内容和他告诉全国的内容是两个不同的故事。”

contentParagraphs.en: Fauci and Paul did not respond to an NPR request for comment prior to publication. The document was taken down on Monday evening and reposted by Tuesday morning with redactions.
contentParagraphs.zh: 福奇和保罗在发表之前没有回应 NPR 的置评请求。该文件于周一晚上被删除，并于周二早上重新发布并进行了编辑。

contentParagraphs.en: Felicia Goodrum, a virologist at Dartmouth College who spoke to NPR from the American Society for Virology meeting in Minneapolis, says that it's possible that Fauci may have been less certain in private with his colleagues as they were racing to learn about the new virus than he was in public where he had to assure a population that was panicking over the rapidly emerging pandemic.
contentParagraphs.zh: 达特茅斯学院的病毒学家费利西亚·古德鲁姆在明尼阿波利斯举行的美国病毒学学会会议上接受美国国家公共广播电台采访时表示，福奇在私下里与他的同事们可能不太确定，因为他们正在竞相了解这种新病毒，而他必须在公共场合向那些对迅速出现的流行病感到恐慌的人们保证。

contentParagraphs.en: For stories of life in our changing world, subscribe here to the global health newsletter.
contentParagraphs.zh: 要了解不断变化的世界中的生活故事，请在此处订阅全球健康通讯。

contentParagraphs.en: This thread emerges ahead of a scheduled hearing on Wednesday before the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul chairs. Paul unilaterally subpoenaed Fauci to testify after he said that Fauci notified the committee that he wouldn't appear voluntarily. Lawmakers are expected to question Fauci about what he knew and didn't know as the pandemic was unfolding.
contentParagraphs.zh: 这条线索是在保罗担任主席的参议院国土安全和政府事务委员会定于周三举行的听证会之前出现的。保罗在表示福奇通知委员会他不会自愿出庭后，单方面传唤福奇作证。随着疫情的发展，预计议员们将向福奇询问他所知道和不知道的事情。

contentParagraphs.en: What is Rand Paul looking to hear from Anthony Fauci?
contentParagraphs.zh: 兰德·保罗希望从安东尼·福奇那里听到什么？

contentParagraphs.en: For years, Paul and Fauci have differed over the origins of SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19. Fauci has asserted that the scientific evidence points to a spillover — whereby the virus would have found its way from an animal into its first human host, and then spread at that point from human to human.
contentParagraphs.zh: 多年来，保罗和福奇对于导致 COVID-19 的病毒 SARS-CoV-2 的起源存在分歧。福奇断言，科学证据表明存在溢出效应——病毒会从动物进入第一个人类宿主，然后在人与人之间传播。

contentParagraphs.en: Proponents of this theory point to the wet market in Wuhan where potentially infected animals were waiting to be sold. "There's very good evidence that there are two lineages [of SARS-CoV-2] that emerged," according to Goodrum. "Both of those lineages were present at the market, and susceptible animals were present at the market."
contentParagraphs.zh: 这一理论的支持者指出，武汉的农贸市场上有可能受感染的动物正在等待出售。古德鲁姆表示：“有非常充分的证据表明[SARS-CoV-2]出现了两个谱系。” “这两个谱系都存在于市场上，并且易感动物也存在于市场上。”

contentParagraphs.en: Goodrum says the market was cleared before it was possible to take any samples. However, she says the genetic data "maps all initial cases to that market" and "none to, for example, the Wuhan Institute of Virology, where they have accused the virus of having been created or released."
contentParagraphs.zh: 古德鲁姆表示，在采集样本之前，市场已被清空。然而，她表示，基因数据“将所有最初病例都映射到该市场”，“没有一个映射到武汉病毒研究所等地方，他们指责该病毒是在那里制造或释放的。”

contentParagraphs.en: Most scientists in the virology community share this view, according to a survey published in February 2024 by the Global Catastrophic Risk Institute, a nonpartisan U.S.-based think tank that studies potentially catastrophic events.
contentParagraphs.zh: 全球灾难风险研究所（一家研究潜在灾难性事件的美国无党派智库）于 2024 年 2 月发布的一项调查显示，病毒学界的大多数科学家都同意这一观点。

contentParagraphs.en: Paul has advocated for an alternative explanation. He says the possibility that the virus was engineered in a lab should not be discounted. Two years ago, during a full Senate committee hearing, Paul said, "Do we know for certain it came from the lab? No, but there's a preponderance of evidence indicating that it may have come from the lab."
contentParagraphs.zh: 保罗主张另一种解释。他说，不应忽视该病毒是在实验室设计的可能性。两年前，在参议院委员会的一次全体听证会上，保罗说：“我们确定它来自实验室吗？不，但有大量证据表明它可能来自实验室。”

contentParagraphs.en: In late 2024, the Republican-led Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus Pandemic published its final report that concluded a lab leak was the most likely explanation for the origins of SARS-CoV-2. They suggested that funds from the NIH may have helped support research by the Wuhan Institute of Virology to make a more potent or transmissible virus. Such viral enhancement is called gain of function.
contentParagraphs.zh: 2024 年底，共和党领导的冠状病毒大流行特别小组委员会发布了最终报告，得出的结论是实验室泄漏是 SARS-CoV-2 起源的最可能解释。他们表示，美国国立卫生研究院的资金可能有助于支持武汉病毒研究所的研究，以制造一种更有效或更具传染性的病毒。这种病毒性增强称为功能获得。

contentParagraphs.en: But Robert Garry, a virologist at Tulane University, says he disputes this line of reasoning because there is "no actual evidence for it." And he says that no one, including the Wuhan Institute of Virology, had a precursor virus similar enough to SARS-CoV-2 to create the pathogen that ultimately caused the pandemic.
contentParagraphs.zh: 但杜兰大学病毒学家罗伯特·加里表示，他对这种推理提出异议，因为“没有实际证据”。他说，包括武汉病毒学研究所在内，没有人拥有与 SARS-CoV-2 足够相似的前体病毒，足以产生最终导致大流行的病原体。

contentParagraphs.en: Still, Paul suggests that Fauci, his colleagues, and certain federal agencies may have covered up any evidence to support the lab leak theory. In his view, he said in that same statement, they "withheld and continue to conceal crucial information from both Congress and the public."
contentParagraphs.zh: 尽管如此，保罗表示，福奇、他的同事和某些联邦机构可能掩盖了任何支持实验室泄漏理论的证据。他在同一份声明中表示，他认为，他们“向国会和公众隐瞒并继续隐瞒重要信息”。

contentParagraphs.en: As noted, NPR reached out to Fauci about Paul's comments, but did not receive a response before publication.
contentParagraphs.zh: 如前所述，美国国家公共广播电台就保罗的评论联系了福奇，但在发表之前没有收到回复。

contentParagraphs.en: What does Paul say these newly published diary entries reveal?
contentParagraphs.zh: 保罗说这些新发表的日记揭示了什么？

contentParagraphs.en: In his posts on X, Paul highlights a few select excerpts from Fauci's notes. For instance, he points to an entry on Jan. 26, 2020, not quite two months before the World Health Organization declared a global pandemic, where Fauci writes, "the first infection was in early December and was not connected to the market. … Now we know the market was not the source, it was the amplifier."
contentParagraphs.zh: 保罗在 X 上的帖子中重点介绍了福奇笔记中的一些精选摘录。例如，他指出了 2020 年 1 月 26 日的一条记录，距离世界卫生组织宣布全球大流行还不到两个月，福奇写道，“第一次感染发生在 12 月初，与市场无关……现在我们知道市场不是源头，而是放大器。”

contentParagraphs.en: Paul notes in his post, "The wet market was already off the table in [Fauci's] own private notes."
contentParagraphs.zh: 保罗在他的帖子中指出，“在[福奇]自己的私人笔记中，生鲜市场已经被排除在外。”

contentParagraphs.en: But in that same journal entry, Fauci adds, "Having said that, somewhere the virus jumped from animals to humans."
contentParagraphs.zh: 但在同一篇日记中，福奇补充道，“话虽如此，病毒在某个地方从动物传染给了人类。”

contentParagraphs.zh: 不到一周后，在二月份写的一篇文章中。
